[Chihuahua tags](https://saltydogtags.com/chihuahua-dog-tags/) · [Yorkie tags](https://saltydogtags.com/yorkie-dog-tags/) · [Pomeranian tags](https://saltydogtags.com/pomeranian-dog-tags/) · [All breeds →](https://saltydogtags.com/dog-tags-by-breed/)

Questions humans ask

## FAQ

Still stuck? [hello@saltydogtags.com](mailto:hello@saltydogtags.com). A human answers. The dogs supervise.

**Can I put a dog tag on my cat?**

Sometimes, if the tag is small and light enough and you attach it to a proper breakaway collar. A full-size dog tag is usually too big and heavy for most cats. If it swings into the food bowl or drags the collar down, size down.

**Should cats wear collars at all if they're indoor-only?**

That's between you and your vet, but plenty of owners put ID on indoor cats because indoor cats are only indoor until somebody leaves the door open. A tag that says "Indoor cat" tells a finder this one escaped. Pair it with a microchip.

**What's the most important thing to engrave on a pet tag?**

A phone number that actually works. Everything else is a bonus. If space is tight, which it often is on cat tags, the phone number wins.

**Are funny tags a good idea, or just cute?**

Both, we'd argue. A tag's job is to get someone to call you. A tag that makes a stranger laugh doesn't hurt that cause. Just keep the phone number clear and readable. The joke is the setup. Getting your pet home is the punchline.

**What tag material holds up best in Florida?**

Florida's salt air, humidity, and beach days are rough on metal. Corrosion-resistant materials and deep, clear engraving tend to hold up better over time. Check rings and hooks periodically, especially on dogs that swim.

# Desert Heat and Your Dog in St. George: Pavement, Cars, Trails and a Tag That Reads

> St. George summer heat and your dog: the pavement test, hot cars, trail timing and water, from NPS, NWS and Utah State Parks, plus a lost-dog plan.

Canonical page: https://saltydogtags.com/guides/desert-heat-dog-safety-st-george/

Salty Dog Tags · Updated Nov 16, 2026

St. George summers are long, bright and hot, and your dog is out in the same sun you are. This page sticks to what park and weather service pages actually say, linked, as checked on 2026-11-16. It isn't veterinary advice. If you think your dog is overheating, call your vet.

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## How hot it gets

Utah State Parks says daytime temperatures at Snow Canyon State Park **frequently top 105 degrees in July and August**. For people, the park's summer advice is to carry and drink water (32 ounces per person, per hour), wear sunscreen, dress for it, and **avoid the hotter hours, 11 a.m. to 7 p.m.**

Your dog doesn't read the sign, so plan its walks around the same hours.

Source: [Snow Canyon State Park current conditions](https://stateparks.utah.gov/parks/snow-canyon/current-conditions/).

## The pavement test

Zion National Park's B.A.R.K. Ranger page puts it simply: "Hot to touch? Too hot for paws!" It says to avoid walking your pet in the heat of the day and gives a **five-second rule**: place the back of your hand on the pavement, and if you can't hold it there for five seconds, it's too hot to walk your pet.

Around town that means sidewalks, parking lots and paved trails. Do the test before you leave the car, not halfway down the block.

Source: [Zion National Park, B.A.R.K. Ranger](https://home.nps.gov/articles/000/zionbarkranger.htm).

## Never in the car

The National Weather Service is blunt: **don't leave pets in cars.** Even in cool temperatures, cars can heat up to dangerous temperatures very quickly, and **even with the windows cracked, the temperature inside can rise almost 20 degrees Fahrenheit in the first 10 minutes.** Any pet left inside is at risk of serious heat-related illness or death.

Zion's pets page says the same about the desert: during most of the year, the inside of a vehicle can quickly warm to dangerous levels. If the plan includes a stop where the dog can't come in, the dog stays home. The park lists boarding kennels in Hurricane, St. George, Kanab, Cedar City and Rockville for park days.

Sources: [National Weather Service pet safety](https://www.weather.gov/mqt/petsafety) and [Zion National Park: pets](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/pets.htm).

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## On the trail: water, water quality, wildlife, weather

- **Water:** "Always carry extra food and water for your pet," says Zion's B.A.R.K. Ranger page. Ask a ranger if you need the closest drinking water.
- **Not that water:** in Zion, keep dogs out of the Virgin River. The park monitors it for toxic cyanobacteria, which can be present at any time of year, and dogs may ingest it.
- **Leash on:** Snow Canyon (6 feet max) and the Red Cliffs Desert Reserve both require a leash. Both warn about rattlesnakes and Gila monsters, and Snow Canyon adds scorpions and spiders. Rules for each place are in our [dog parks and trails guide](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/st-george-dog-parks-and-trails/#snow-canyon).
- **Monsoon:** Snow Canyon says the summer monsoon season usually runs July through September, with the potential for heavy afternoon rain and flash floods.

Sources: [Zion B.A.R.K. Ranger](https://home.nps.gov/articles/000/zionbarkranger.htm), [Zion: pets](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/pets.htm), [Snow Canyon State Park](https://stateparks.utah.gov/parks/snow-canyon/) and [Red Cliffs Desert Reserve rules](https://www.redcliffsdesertreserve.com/rules).

## If your dog gets loose in the heat

This is where the tag earns its spot on the collar. A loose dog on a July afternoon needs to get home quickly, and shelters keep office hours:

- **St. George Animal Shelter:** by appointment only, Monday to Saturday; closed Sunday. 435-627-4350. ([city page](https://www.sgcityutah.gov/departments/police_department/animal_services___shelter.php))
- **Washington City Animal Shelter:** Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.; closed weekends and holidays. (435) 673-7194. ([city page](https://washingtonutah.gov/services/publicsafety/police/animalwelfare))
- **Hurricane Animal Shelter:** 435-635-8314. ([city page](https://www.cityofhurricane.com/159/Animal-Control-Shelter))
- **Santa Clara–Ivins Animal Control:** 435-628-1049. ([Ivins Public Safety](https://ivinsutah.gov/public-safety-3/))

A finder who can read your phone number on the tag can call you at 2 p.m. on a Sunday. A finder who can only read a license number has to wait for an office to open. So:

- **Phone number first and biggest**, then the dog's name. A second number helps if you hike where your phone has no signal.
- **Engraved**, so the number is cut into the metal rather than printed on top. Our guide to [whether dog tags wear off](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/do-dog-tags-wear-off/) compares the methods.
- **Keep the license tag current too.** In St. George, renewals are due by February 28; our [license rules guide](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/st-george-dog-license-rules/) has every city's dates.

Optional backup: on tags that support it, a $5 scan-to-find QR on the back opens a finder page for your dog, with email alerts to you once you activate it. Keep the number engraved anyway. A QR needs a signal, and trails don't always have one.

## Quick summer checklist

- Walk early or late, and do the five-second pavement test first.
- Never leave the dog in the car, windows cracked or not.
- Carry water for the dog on every trail, and keep it out of the Virgin River in Zion.
- Use a 6-foot leash on Snow Canyon and Red Cliffs trails.
- Make sure the ID tag has a phone number a stranger can read. [Build one here](https://saltydogtags.com/#build), or browse our [St. George sayings](https://saltydogtags.com/st-george-dog-tags/#st-george-sayings-grid).

- [Free**Roast my dog →** — One photo and a name. We write the jokes, you pick one for the tag.](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/)
- [From $12**Build a tag →** — Pick a line or write your own. Name and number go on the back.](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)

[Dog tags for St. George →](https://saltydogtags.com/st-george-dog-tags/)

*This article is general information, not legal or veterinary advice. Rules are set city by city and by each park, and they change. Check the linked page or call the office before you rely on anything here. Last checked 2026-11-16.*

**How hot does it get in St. George in summer?**

Utah State Parks says daytime temperatures at Snow Canyon State Park frequently top 105 degrees Fahrenheit in July and August.

**How do I know if the pavement is too hot for my dog?**

Zion National Park's B.A.R.K. Ranger page gives a five-second rule: place the back of your hand on the pavement, and if you cannot hold it there for five seconds, it's too hot to walk your pet.

**Can I leave my dog in the car with the windows cracked?**

The National Weather Service says no: even with the windows cracked, the temperature inside a car can rise almost 20 degrees Fahrenheit in the first 10 minutes, and any pet left inside is at risk.

**What should a dog tag say for desert hikes?**

Your phone number first, big enough to read at arm's length, with the dog's name. A finder on a hot trail can call you right away, which matters when shelters are closed or by appointment only.

**Is this veterinary advice?**

No. It's what the park and weather service pages say, linked. If you think your dog is overheating, call your vet.

# Do Dog Tags Wear Off? Engraving vs. Printing, and What Actually Lasts

> Do dog tags wear off? How engraving, printing, and stamping hold up to sand, salt water, concrete, and bulldogs who drag their chins everywhere.

Canonical page: https://saltydogtags.com/guides/do-dog-tags-wear-off/

Salty Dog Tags · Updated Oct 12, 2026

Short answer: yes. Dog tags wear off. Everything wears off. Your dog's tag lives a harder life than your car keys. It gets dragged across sidewalks, dunked in the Gulf, rolled in sand, chewed by a sibling, and clanked against a water bowl roughly a thousand times a day.

We run Salty Dog Tags out of Lehi, Utah, with seven English bulldogs supervising operations. "Supervising" means snoring, mostly. Bulldogs are basically tag-destruction test units. They're low to the ground, they drag their chins on everything, and they lie face-down on concrete like it owes them money. If a tag can survive a bulldog, it can survive your dog.

So let's talk about what makes a tag fade, what makes it last, and why the method used to put words on metal matters more than most people think.

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## The Short Answer: Some Tags Wear Out Way Faster Than Others

Every tag eventually shows its age. What matters is whether your phone number is still readable when a stranger finds your dog behind a Publix at 9 p.m.

How long the text survives depends on two things:

- **How the text was applied.** Printed, stamped, or engraved.
- **What the tag is made of.** Aluminum, stainless steel, brass, plastic, and so on.

A pretty tag with an unreadable phone number is just jewelry. Your dog does not need jewelry. Your dog needs a way home.

## What Actually Destroys a Dog Tag

Before comparing methods, it helps to know what you're up against. Tags don't fade from old age. They get worn down by contact, a little at a time.

- **Sand.** If you're in Florida, this is enemy number one. Sand is basically sandpaper that hasn't been glued down yet. A tag that spends weekends at the beach gets scuffed constantly.
- **Salt water.** It's hard on some metals and on cheap coatings. Then the salt dries in the grooves and keeps grinding.
- **Pavement and concrete.** Short-legged dogs, flat-faced dogs, and dogs who flop dramatically onto the driveway all scrape their tags on the ground.
- **Other tags.** The rabies tag, the license tag, and the ID tag spend all day banging into each other. That jingle you hear is your tags slowly sanding each other down.
- **Chewing.** Siblings chew on each other's collars. Some dogs chew their own tags. We don't judge. We just notice.
- **Pool chemicals and sun.** Chlorinated pools and constant UV exposure can be rough on printed surfaces and colored finishes.

Any one of these is manageable. A Florida dog deals with all of them before lunch.

## Printed Dog Tags: Pretty Until They Aren't

Printed tags have ink or a coating sitting on the surface of the metal. Common methods include UV printing and dye sublimation onto coated blanks. They can look great when they're new, with full color, photos, and gradients. Very Instagram.

The catch is that the design sits *on* the tag, not *in* it. Whatever scrapes the surface scrapes the design too.

**Where printed tags struggle:**

- Surface scratches go straight through the artwork and text.
- Tag-on-tag rubbing wears down high spots and edges first.
- Sand and pavement can scuff fine details, and small text goes first. Small text is usually your phone number.
- Some printed finishes can fade or dull with long sun exposure.

Printed tags aren't automatically bad. A quality printed tag on a mellow indoor cat that naps on a velvet pillow might look fine for a long time. But for a dog who treats the beach as a contact sport, surface-printed text is the weak point.

## Laser Engraving: Changing the Metal Itself

This is what we do, so yes, we have opinions. We'll try to keep them honest.

Laser engraving uses a focused beam to change the surface of the material. It doesn't add anything on top. Depending on the metal, that works a few different ways:

- **Anodized aluminum:** Colored aluminum tags have a thin anodized layer. The laser removes that layer where the text goes and exposes the bright metal underneath. The result is crisp, high-contrast text, like silver lettering on a colored tag.
- **Stainless steel:** A laser can either mark the surface (a darkened mark created by heat) or cut into it more deeply, depending on settings and equipment.
- **Other metals and coated tags:** Results vary with the material and finish. Laser engraving isn't magic. It's physics with a really good aim.

**Why it holds up better:** No ink is sitting on the surface waiting to get scraped off. The text is part of the tag. A scratch across an engraved tag is just a scratch. It doesn't peel the letters off with it.

**Being honest about the limits:** Engraved tags still wear. On anodized aluminum, heavy rubbing can scuff the colored finish around the letters, so the tag looks worn sooner than stainless. The letters themselves are bright bare metal, so they stay readable. Very shallow marks can soften with heavy abrasion. And aluminum is a softer metal, so a dedicated chewer can leave dents. Engraving tends to outlast surface printing, but it doesn't make a tag immortal. Nothing survives a bulldog forever. We've checked.

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## Hand-Stamped and Deep-Engraved Tags

**Hand-stamped tags** have letters punched into the metal with steel stamps and a hammer. The letters are physically pressed into the tag, so they're very durable. Stamped tags tend to have a rustic, slightly uneven look, which some people love. They're also usually limited to simple text with fewer design options.

**Deep or rotary engraving** cuts a groove into the metal with a tool. Mall-kiosk tag machines often work this way, using a diamond-tipped or rotary bit. Grooves can be fairly durable, though cheaper machines may produce shallow, wobbly lines.

Both methods can last a long time. Stamped grooves can fill with dirt and grime, which sometimes helps readability and sometimes just makes the tag look like it's been to a mud run.

## Material Matters as Much as Method

A great engraving on a flimsy tag is still a flimsy tag. In short: stainless steel is the toughest and handles salt water best, aluminum is light and takes bright color but dents and scratches more easily, and brass looks classic but tarnishes. We compared all three, bulldog-tested, in [Stainless vs. Aluminum vs. Brass Dog Tags](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/stainless-vs-aluminum-vs-brass-dog-tags/).

For beach dogs, swimmers, and dogs who live outdoors, a corrosion-resistant metal with engraved text is usually the safest bet. For the couch-bound, almost anything works, as long as it stays readable.

## How to Tell Your Dog's Tag Is About to Fail

Check your dog's tag every so often. Bath day is a good reminder. Look for these warning signs:

- **You have to squint to read the phone number.** If you have to squint, a stranger in a parking lot won't bother.
- **Edges are worn smooth** or the letters look "soft."
- **The colored finish is mostly gone** and the text is losing contrast.
- **The ring hole is stretched or thin.** This is a sneaky one. A tag with perfect text is useless if it falls off the collar.
- **The split ring is bent open.** Same problem.
- **Your info changed.** You moved, or got a new number, or the old number belongs to your ex now. Update the tag.

## How to Make Any Dog Tag Last Longer

You can't stop a bulldog from lying face-first on the patio. You can cut down on the damage.

- **Rinse after the beach or pool.** A quick freshwater rinse gets salt, sand, and chlorine off the tag before they keep working on it.
- **Use a tag silencer or a slide-on tag.** Silencers wrap around the tag and cut down on tag-on-tag grinding. They also save your sanity at 3 a.m.
- **Separate the tags.** If your dog wears several, spreading them out means less metal rubbing on metal.
- **Check the ring and attachment.** Swap out worn split rings before they fail.
- **Pick the right material for the dog.** Chewers and swimmers deserve tougher tags. Senior couch potatoes can wear whatever they like.
- **Keep the critical info big and clear.** A phone number in large, simple type stays readable longer than tiny decorative script.

## What to Engrave So It Still Works When It's Worn

Durability isn't only about metal. It's also about what you put on the tag. Priorities:

- **Phone number first.** Make it big and clear. More on this in [what to put on a dog tag](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/what-to-put-on-a-dog-tag/). This is the line that gets your dog home.
- **Dog's name.** Optional, but helpful.
- **A line that makes people want to help.** This is where we come in.

A finder who smiles is a finder who calls. A tag that says *"Not lost. Taking a tour."* or *"Don't follow me. I'm lost too."* tells a stranger this dog is loved, a little ridiculous, and worth a phone call. Our bulldogs would wear *"Built for comfort, not speed."* and *"Runs on naps and spite."* with pride, if they ever woke up.

Just keep the joke from crowding out the phone number. The joke is the hook. The number is the point.

Seven bulldogs have tested every way a tag can get scuffed, dunked, and drooled on, so we laser-engrave ours to stay readable. Find one that fits your dog's personality in [the builder](https://saltydogtags.com/#build). Snoring sold separately.

Questions humans ask

## FAQ

Still stuck? [hello@saltydogtags.com](mailto:hello@saltydogtags.com). A human answers. The dogs supervise.

**Do engraved dog tags fade?**

Engraved text doesn't fade the way ink does, because the text is part of the metal and not a layer on top. On colored aluminum, heavy scraping can scuff the finish around the letters, but the letters are bare metal and stay readable. Check your tag now and then, and replace it when the phone number gets hard to read.

**Are printed dog tags waterproof?**

Many printed tags handle water fine at first. The bigger issue is abrasion. Sand, pavement, and other tags can scratch through surface-printed designs. For dogs who swim a lot or spend time on the beach, engraved text is usually the more durable choice.

**What dog tag material is best for Florida beaches?**

Corrosion-resistant metals like stainless steel hold up well to salt water and humidity. Anodized aluminum is a lighter option that also handles moisture well, though it scratches more easily. Whatever you pick, rinse the tag after beach days.

**How often should I replace my dog's tag?**

There's no set schedule. Replace it when the phone number gets hard to read, the ring hole looks worn, or your contact info changes. Checking it on bath day is an easy habit to build.

**Do tag silencers really help tags last longer?**

They cut down on direct metal-on-metal rubbing between tags, which is one of the main causes of wear. They also make your dog quieter, which nobody in your house will complain about.

# Dog Birthday Ideas (From a House With Seven Bulldogs and Zero Chill)

> Dog birthday ideas from a family with seven English bulldogs: dog-safe cakes, party plans, beach days, gifts, and how to skip the chaos.

Canonical page: https://saltydogtags.com/guides/dog-birthday-ideas/

Salty Dog Tags · Updated Oct 12, 2026

Your dog does not know it's their birthday. Your dog does not know what a birthday *is*. Your dog thinks Tuesday is a concept you made up to keep them from the couch.

Celebrate anyway.

We're a family with seven English bulldogs, which means we throw a dog birthday party roughly every seven weeks and have learned a few things the hard way. Party hats last about four seconds. Cake gets eaten off the floor. And the birthday dog usually naps through the best part.

Here's how to plan a dog birthday that's fun for the dog, survivable for you, and worth a few photos, whether you're doing a sunrise beach day in Florida or a living room party while it snows in Utah.

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## First, Figure Out What Kind of Birthday Your Dog Actually Wants

Some dogs want a party. Some dogs want you to leave them alone with a bully stick and a closed door. Plan for the dog you have, not the dog on Instagram.

Ask yourself honestly:

- **Does your dog like other dogs?** If the answer is "some of them, on a good day," skip the 12-dog guest list.
- **Does your dog like people?** Or do they bark at the mail carrier like he owes them money?
- **How does your dog handle heat?** This matters a lot if you're in Florida, and it's non-negotiable if you own a flat-faced breed. More on that below.
- **What does your dog love most?** Food, fetch, sniffing, napping, or being held like a baby. Build the day around that.

Our bulldogs are simple. Their ideal birthday is a snack, a nap, another snack, and a slow walk where they stop to smell every mailbox like it's a fine wine. Honestly, same.

## Make a Dog-Safe Birthday Cake (Not the One From the Grocery Store)

Human birthday cake is a bad idea for dogs. Sugar, frosting, and some common ingredients can range from "upset stomach" to "emergency vet visit." Make something dog-friendly instead. It's easy and your dog won't judge your piping skills.

**A simple dog birthday cake idea:**

- Plain canned pumpkin (not pumpkin pie filling, which has spices and sugar)
- Peanut butter, but **only** a brand with no xylitol. Check the label every single time. Xylitol is seriously dangerous for dogs.
- An egg
- A little whole wheat or oat flour
- Mashed banana or unsweetened applesauce if you want it sweeter

Mix it, bake it in a small pan or muffin tin until it's cooked through, and let it cool completely. For "frosting," use plain unsweetened yogurt or a smear of that xylitol-free peanut butter.

**Keep these out of the cake (and away from the party table):**

- Chocolate
- Grapes and raisins
- Onions and garlic
- Xylitol (also called birch sugar)
- Macadamia nuts
- Anything with alcohol, including your margarita, Kevin

If your dog has allergies, a sensitive stomach, or a medical condition, check with your vet before you go wild. And remember a birthday cake is a treat, not dinner. A small slice is plenty. A bulldog will tell you otherwise. A bulldog is lying.

## Dog Birthday Party Ideas That Won't End in a Vet Visit

### The Beach Birthday (Florida Edition)

If you live near the coast, a beach birthday is hard to beat. Sand, sniffs, and that one seagull your dog will never catch.

A few ground rules:

- **Find a dog-friendly beach first.** Not every beach allows dogs, and the rules can change by area and season. Check the local regulations before you load up the car.
- **Go early.** Sunrise or early morning is the move. Midday sand can burn paws, and Florida heat doesn't care that it's a special occasion.
- **Bring shade and fresh water.** Dogs shouldn't drink salt water, no matter how confidently they try.
- **Life vest for non-swimmers.** Bulldogs, for example, are built like cinder blocks with feelings. Many bulldogs can't swim. Ours still insist on going to the beach. *"Can't swim. Still at the beach."* is a tag for a reason.
- **Rinse off afterward.** Salt and sand in fur and paws gets itchy fast.

### The Backyard Sniff Party

Invite a few dog friends your pup actually likes. Set out water bowls, a kiddie pool if it's warm, some shade, and a few toys. Keep it short. An hour of fun beats three hours of overstimulated dogs deciding who owns the tennis ball.

Pro tip: put away high-value toys and chews beforehand. Nothing ruins a party faster than a resource-guarding standoff over a squeaky hot dog.

### The Indoor Party (For Heat Waves, Snow Days, and Introverts)

Florida in August and Utah in January have one thing in common: sometimes the best party is inside. Crank the AC (or the heat), lay out blankets, and turn your living room into a birthday lounge. Add a puzzle toy, a frozen treat, and a movie you'll watch while your dog snores through it.

Flat-faced breeds like bulldogs, pugs, and Frenchies can overheat easily, so for them, indoor isn't the backup plan. Sometimes it's the plan. We have seven bulldogs. Our birthday parties are heavily air-conditioned.

### The Pup Cup Tour

Plenty of coffee shops and ice cream spots have dog treats or will give your pup a small cup of something. Make a little tour of it. Keep portions small, since dairy doesn't sit well with every dog. Bring a towel for the face. You'll need the towel.

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## Birthday Games and Activities

You don't need a full party to make the day feel special. These work for a party of one dog and one tired human:

- **Treat hunt.** Hide small treats around the yard or house and let your dog sniff them out. Sniffing is real work for a dog's brain, and a great way to tire out a dog who doesn't love running.
- **Snuffle mat or puzzle toy.** Put their birthday breakfast in it. Instant enrichment.
- **A brand-new walk.** Take a route your dog has never been on. New smells are basically a birthday card.
- **Frozen treat.** Freeze plain yogurt, pumpkin, or dog-safe broth in a toy or ice cube tray. Great for hot days.
- **"Yes Day."** Within reason. Yes to the extra cuddle. Yes to the couch. No to the trash can, no matter how persuasive they are.
- **A game they love.** Fetch, tug, chase, or lying on top of you like a weighted blanket with bad breath.

## Dog Birthday Gift Ideas That Aren't Just Another Squeaky Toy

Your dog has toys. Your dog has destroyed toys. Here are gift ideas that last longer than four minutes:

- **A new ID tag.** Every dog needs one, and a birthday is a great excuse to swap out the scratched-up tag from three addresses ago. Make sure it has a working phone number (here's [what to put on a dog tag](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/what-to-put-on-a-dog-tag/)). Make it funny if you want. A tag that says *"Firstborn. Still the favorite."* or *"Grandma's favorite."* is a birthday gift and a family announcement in one.
- **A comfortable bed.** Especially for senior dogs or breeds that treat napping as a career. (*"Built for comfort, not speed."*)
- **Enrichment toys.** Lick mats, snuffle mats, and puzzle feeders give your dog something to do besides judging you.
- **A cooling mat.** Practical for Florida summers and any breed that overheats easily.
- **A professional grooming day.** Or a bath at home and a very dramatic towel-off.
- **Quality time.** Yes, it's cheesy. It's also what they actually want.

Since we laser-engrave our tags in-house, we may be biased about the tag thing. But a fresh, readable tag with current contact info is one of the most useful things you can give your dog, and it's the only birthday gift they'll wear every day. The toy will be in pieces by Thursday.

## Dog Birthday Photos: Lower Your Expectations

You will picture a perfect shot. Your dog in a tiny hat, sitting politely next to a cake, gazing into the camera like a professional.

You will get this instead: a blurry ear, a tongue, the back of a head, and one photo where your dog is mid-sneeze.

A few tips to help:

- **Take photos before the cake.** Once there's food involved, your dog's attention is gone.
- **Use treats behind the camera.** Hold one right above the lens for that "looking at you" shot.
- **Natural light wins.** Early morning or late afternoon, outdoors or near a window.
- **Skip anything they hate.** If the hat makes them miserable, ditch the hat. A bandana is a fine compromise.
- **Take a lot.** One will be good. Probably.

Honestly, the sneeze photo will end up being your favorite.

## Don't Know Your Dog's Birthday? Pick One.

Rescue dogs often come without a birth certificate, and that's fine. Plenty of people celebrate their dog's "Gotcha Day," the day they came home. Others pick a date that means something to the family, or just pick a day and commit.

Your dog won't fact-check you. They're too busy being lovable and slightly unhinged.

Whatever you plan, keep it simple, safe, and about your dog. And if they need a fresh tag for their next trip around the sun, we've got a few with plenty of attitude in [the builder](https://saltydogtags.com/#build).

- [From $12**Build a tag →** — Pick a line or write your own. Name and number go on the back.](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)

Questions humans ask

## FAQ

Still stuck? [hello@saltydogtags.com](mailto:hello@saltydogtags.com). A human answers. The dogs supervise.

**What can dogs eat on their birthday?**

Dog-safe options include plain pumpkin, xylitol-free peanut butter, plain unsweetened yogurt in small amounts, banana, and dog-specific treats. Avoid chocolate, grapes, raisins, onions, garlic, xylitol, and regular frosted birthday cake. If your dog has dietary issues, ask your vet first.

**How do I throw a dog birthday party in the Florida heat?**

Go early in the morning or later in the evening, keep plenty of fresh water and shade on hand, and watch for signs of overheating like heavy panting or sluggishness. For flat-faced breeds or hot days in general, an air-conditioned indoor party is often the smarter call.

**How many dogs should I invite to a dog birthday party?**

Only as many as your dog actually enjoys being around, and only dogs who already get along. A small group of familiar friends is usually more fun (and much less chaotic) than a big crowd of strangers.

**What's a good birthday gift for a dog?**

Practical gifts that get used: a new ID tag with current contact info, an enrichment toy, a comfy bed, or a cooling mat. Add a fun walk or extra cuddle time and you've nailed it.

**What if I don't know my dog's real birthday?**

Celebrate their adoption day ("Gotcha Day") or choose a date that works for your family. The point is celebrating your dog, not the calendar.

# Dog Parks in Utah County (and Draper), Checked Against City Pages

> Off-leash dog parks in Utah County and Draper, from city pages: Lehi, Saratoga Springs, Orem, Provo. Hours, closures and where leashes are the rule.

Canonical page: https://saltydogtags.com/guides/dog-parks-utah-county/

Salty Dog Tags · Updated Oct 13, 2026

Utah County is mostly a leash-required place. Off-leash means a designated dog park, and most cities have exactly one or two. Here's what each city's own page says, as checked on 2026-10-13. If a city didn't publish hours or rules, we say so instead of making them up.

A loose dog in a dog park is a feature. A loose dog outside one is a phone call. Make sure it's yours that rings: [put your number on a tag](https://saltydogtags.com/#build).

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## Lehi: Willow Park and Exchange Park

- Lehi has **two dedicated dog parks: Willow Park and Exchange Park**. Every other city park requires a leash.
- **No dogs at all** at Lehi Sports Park or Veterans Memorial Ball Park.
- Most Lehi parks are open 5 AM to 11 PM, and parks can't be occupied 11 PM to 5 AM.
- Willow Park's dog park sits next to the Willow Park campground, 2998 West 300 North. Willow Park itself is open 7 AM to 10 PM.

Sources: [Lehi parks FAQ](https://www.lehi-ut.gov/recreation-community/parks-trails/faqs), [Willow Park](https://www.lehi-ut.gov/recreation-community/parks-trails/parks/willow-park/).

## Saratoga Springs: Saratoga Ridge Park

- The dog park is at the south end of **Saratoga Ridge Park**, 532 N Mount Saratoga Blvd.
- The park is open 6 AM to 10 PM.
- The dog park is **closed the 2nd and 4th Tuesdays** of each month for maintenance.
- Water fountains, including the dog park's, are winterized October 15 to April 15. Bring water. Bulldogs especially.

Source: [Saratoga Ridge Park](https://www.saratogasprings-ut.gov/Facilities/Facility/Details/Saratoga-Ridge-Park-68).

## Orem: Timpanogos Park

Orem's animal control page names the dog park area at **Timpanogos Park** as the city park where dogs can run free. It doesn't list hours or rules, so call the city before your first visit.

Source: [Orem City Animal Control](https://orem.gov/animal-control/).

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## Provo: Bicentennial Park

Provo's park guidelines name the designated **dog park inside Bicentennial Park** as the city's off-leash area. Check provo.gov for hours and current rules.

Source: [Provo Parks Use Guidelines (PDF)](https://www.provo.gov/DocumentCenter/View/1184/Parks-Use-Guidelines-PDF).

## Draper (Salt Lake County, but close enough)

- Designated off-leash areas: **Dayland Dog Park**, **Galena Dog Park** and the **West Bluff** off-leash test area at 1455 E. Deer Ridge Drive.
- Dogs are allowed **on leash** on the Bonneville Shoreline Trail and the trails below it.
- Dogs are **not allowed** in the Corner Canyon watershed area above the Bonneville Shoreline Trail.

Source: [Draper rules and trail etiquette](https://www.draperutah.gov/living-in-draper-city/parks-and-trails/rules-trail-etiquette/).

## American Fork and everywhere else

We couldn't find an official city page listing a designated off-leash park for American Fork, Pleasant Grove or the other cities, so they're not on this list yet. Check your city's parks page or call the parks office before you unclip.

## St. George and Washington County

Heading south? We checked the fenced dog parks in St. George, Washington City and Hurricane, plus the leash rules for Snow Canyon, Red Cliffs and Zion, in [St. George dog parks and dog-friendly trails](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/st-george-dog-parks-and-trails/).

- Bring a leash even to the dog park. You'll need it in the parking lot.
- Bring water, bags and a dog who comes back when called. Two out of three is typical.
- Get your dog licensed (here are the [Utah license rules](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/utah-dog-license-and-tag-rules/)) and wearing an ID tag with your phone number.

# Dog Tag Size Guide by Breed: Pick the Right Fit (Then Pick the Right Insult)

> Small, medium, or large? Our breed-by-breed dog tag size guide helps you pick the right fit, from Chihuahuas to bulldogs to giants. Engraved with sass.

Canonical page: https://saltydogtags.com/guides/dog-tag-size-guide-by-breed/

Update: each shape now comes in one size, so you pick the shape and the size comes with it. Read the sizes below as a guide to the shape: small is the round (about 1.2 inches), medium is the bone, heart or paw (about 1.5 inches), large is the military (about 2 inches), and the polished stainless bone is the biggest at 48 mm. Prices are on each shape in the [builder](https://saltydogtags.com/#build).

Salty Dog Tags · Updated Oct 12, 2026

Here's the thing nobody tells you about dog tags: size matters. A tag that's too big on a tiny dog looks like a dinner plate, and a tag that's too small on a big dog disappears into the neck folds. Ask us how we know. We live with seven English bulldogs in Lehi, Utah, and between them there are more neck folds than a shar-pei convention.

So before you fall in love with a tag that says "Certified menace," let's make sure it actually fits the menace in question.

This guide walks through our three tag sizes (small, medium, and large), which breeds usually land where, and how to decide when your dog refuses to fit neatly into a category. Which, let's be honest, is most dogs.

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## Our Dog Tag Sizes at a Glance

Keeping it simple. Every Salty Dog Tag is laser engraved, so your dog's personal brand of chaos stays readable whether they spend their days rolling in Florida beach sand or rolling in whatever that was in the backyard.

| Size | Diameter | Price | Usually Best For

| Small | 1 inch | $12 | Toy and small breeds, puppies

| Medium | 1.5 inch | $14 | Medium breeds, stocky small-to-mid dogs

| Large | 2 inch | $16 | Large and giant breeds, English bulldogs

That's it. Three sizes. No 47-option dropdown menu. You have a dog to chase.

## How to Choose a Dog Tag Size (Before Choosing a Breed)

Breed is a great starting point, but it's not the whole story. A few things matter more than what the shelter paperwork says:

**1. Your dog's neck and collar.** A tag should hang comfortably without smacking your dog in the chin or dragging around like an anchor. Look at the collar width and how much neck real estate you're working with.

**2. How much you want to say.** A short punchline like "Snorts. Means it." fits beautifully on a smaller tag. If your dog's personality requires a three-line setup and payoff, more surface area helps. Type the line into [the builder](https://saltydogtags.com/#build) and the preview shows what fits before you pay.

**3. Your dog's lifestyle.** Couch potato? Beach bum? Professional escape artist? A tag on a dog that's constantly digging, swimming, or sprinting through brush needs to be easy to read when a stranger finally catches them.

**4. Your dog's ego.** Some small dogs simply need a bigger tag. They know who they are. Respect it.

## Small Tags (1 inch, $12): Toy and Small Breeds

The small tag is built for the little ones: the lap dogs, the purse riders, the five-pound tyrants who run the whole house.

**Breeds that usually fit a small tag:**

- [Chihuahua](https://saltydogtags.com/chihuahua-dog-tags/)
- [Yorkshire Terrier](https://saltydogtags.com/yorkie-dog-tags/)
- [Pomeranian](https://saltydogtags.com/pomeranian-dog-tags/)
- Maltese
- [Toy Poodle](https://saltydogtags.com/poodle-dog-tags/)
- Papillon
- [Shih Tzu](https://saltydogtags.com/shih-tzu-dog-tags/)
- [Miniature Dachshund](https://saltydogtags.com/dachshund-dog-tags/)
(standards go Medium)
- Italian Greyhound
- Toy and miniature mixes

A 1-inch tag gives a tiny dog plenty of room to make a statement without dragging their whole head toward the floor. It's also a solid pick for puppies of nearly any breed while they grow into their paws and their attitude.

**Tag lines that hit right on small dogs:**

- "Small dog. Big mouth."
- "Small. Loud. Deeply loved."
- "Velcro dog. Will not detach."

Small dogs are often the ones slipping through gaps in the fence or bolting out the door when the delivery guy shows up. A readable tag is a big deal for a dog that's easy to miss.

## Medium Tags (1.5 inch, $14): The Sweet Spot

The medium tag is the middle child: dependable, easy to get along with, and secretly carrying the whole family. It works for a wide range of dogs, and it gives you a bit more room for those multi-line zingers.

**Breeds that usually fit a medium tag:**

- [French Bulldog](https://saltydogtags.com/frenchie-dog-tags/)
- [Pug](https://saltydogtags.com/pug-dog-tags/)
- [Beagle](https://saltydogtags.com/beagle-dog-tags/)
- [Cavalier King Charles Spaniel](https://saltydogtags.com/cavalier-dog-tags/)
- Cocker Spaniel
- [Corgi](https://saltydogtags.com/corgi-dog-tags/)
(Pembroke and Cardigan)
- [Boston Terrier](https://saltydogtags.com/boston-terrier-dog-tags/)
- Border Collie
- [Australian Shepherd](https://saltydogtags.com/aussie-dog-tags/)
- Shiba Inu
- Standard Schnauzer
- Most medium-sized mixes

**A note on Frenchies and Pugs:** They're compact, but they're built like little bricks. Some owners go small, but many find a medium looks more proportional on that thick neck. If your dog is short but wide, medium is usually your friend.

**Tag lines that hit right on medium dogs:**

- "Built for comfort, not speed."
- "Return for reward. Reward is me."
- "Does not come when called. Try snacks."

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## Our Very Biased Bulldog Section

We have seven English bulldogs. We have opinions.

Bulldogs are a special sizing case because they're medium in height and heavyweight in everything else. Their necks are thick, their chests are broad, and their chins sit low, which means a tag hangs differently on them than on a leggy dog of similar weight.

For most adult English Bulldogs, **large (2 inch)** is the move. It's what we put on our own seven: big enough to read through the jowl-and-fold situation and proportional to that barrel body. A 1-inch tag disappears on a wide bulldog collar. Puppies and lighter-collared bulldogs can start on medium. More in our [bulldog tag guide](https://saltydogtags.com/bulldog-dog-tags/).

What we can tell you from daily life: bulldogs flop. They flop on the couch, flop on the kitchen tile, flop dramatically mid-walk because they've decided they're done. Whatever size you choose, make sure the tag hangs freely when your dog is lying in their natural habitat (horizontal).

**Bulldog-approved lines:**

- "I snore. It's not a medical thing."
- "Runs on naps and spite."
- "Can't swim. Still at the beach."
- "Snores louder than dad."

That last one is a household favorite. Accurate, too.

## Large Tags: Big Dogs, Big Statements

The large tag (2 inch, $16) is for dogs who take up the whole bed and somehow still look offended when you ask for some space.

**Breeds that usually fit a large tag:**

- [English Bulldog](https://saltydogtags.com/bulldog-dog-tags/)
- [Labrador Retriever](https://saltydogtags.com/lab-dog-tags/)
- [Golden Retriever](https://saltydogtags.com/golden-retriever-dog-tags/)
- [German Shepherd](https://saltydogtags.com/german-shepherd-dog-tags/)
- [Boxer](https://saltydogtags.com/boxer-dog-tags/)
- [Doberman Pinscher](https://saltydogtags.com/doberman-dog-tags/)
- [Rottweiler](https://saltydogtags.com/rottweiler-dog-tags/)
- [Siberian Husky](https://saltydogtags.com/husky-dog-tags/)
- [Bernese Mountain Dog](https://saltydogtags.com/bernese-dog-tags/)
- [Great Dane](https://saltydogtags.com/great-dane-dog-tags/)
- [Goldendoodle and Labradoodle](https://saltydogtags.com/doodle-dog-tags/)
- Mastiff
- Newfoundland
- Saint Bernard
- Large and giant mixes

On a big dog, a small tag tends to vanish into fur, especially on fluffy breeds like [Bernese](https://saltydogtags.com/bernese-dog-tags/) and [Huskies](https://saltydogtags.com/husky-dog-tags/). A large tag stays visible and gives a stranger an easier read when your 100-pound "lap dog" knocks them over to say hello.

**Tag lines that hit right on big dogs:**

- "Good boy (legally disputed)."
- "Outside is overrated. Take me home."
- "I know I'm cute. Call my mom anyway."

## What If My Dog Is Between Sizes?

Welcome to the club. Mixed breeds, lanky teenagers, and "the shelter said he'd stay small" dogs all live here.

A few quick rules of thumb:

- **Thin neck, light frame?** Size down.
- **Thick neck, stocky build?** Size up.
- **Long-haired or fluffy?** Size up, so the tag doesn't get lost in the floof.
- **Still growing?** Go with what fits now. You'll want a new tag eventually anyway, because your dog's personality will have evolved into something even more unhinged.
- **Can't decide?** Look at the collar. If the tag would look like a hubcap on it, size down. If it would look like a shirt button, size up.

## Puppies: Size for Now, Not Forever

Puppies grow fast. A Great Dane pup who fits a small tag today will need a large before you've finished house-training. That's fine. Get the tag that fits the dog in front of you, not the dog they'll become.

Bonus: you get to update the joke as they grow. A puppy wearing "Professional snuggler" might graduate to "Certified menace" by the time they've eaten their first shoe.

Got the size figured out? Now for the fun part: finding the line that says exactly what your dog would say if they could talk (and weren't busy napping). Browse [every saying](https://saltydogtags.com/sayings/) or [build a tag](https://saltydogtags.com/#build). Laser engraved, bulldog tested, salt included.

Questions humans ask

## FAQ

Still stuck? [hello@saltydogtags.com](mailto:hello@saltydogtags.com). A human answers. The dogs supervise.

**What size dog tag does my dog need?**

Start with breed as a general guide: small (1 inch, $12) for toy and small breeds, medium (1.5 inch, $14) for medium breeds, and large (2 inch, $16) for big dogs and stocky heavyweights like English bulldogs. Then adjust for neck thickness, coat, and how much text you want on the tag.

**What size tag is best for an English Bulldog?**

Large (2 inch) for most adult English Bulldogs. It's what we put on our own seven: their thick necks and wide collars make a smaller tag disappear. Puppies can start on medium.

**Can a small dog wear a medium tag?**

Sure, if it fits comfortably and doesn't bang into their chin or chest. Some stocky small breeds, like Pugs and Frenchies, look great in medium. Very tiny dogs, like Chihuahuas, are usually happier with a small.

**Does the tag size affect how much text I can fit?**

Generally, a bigger tag gives you more room. Short punchlines fit any size, while longer setups and multi-line jokes have more breathing room on medium or large. The builder preview shows exactly what fits.

**Should I buy a bigger tag for my puppy to grow into?**

We'd skip it. An oversized tag on a small puppy can be clunky and annoying for them. Get the size that fits now and upgrade later. Your dog's attitude will probably need a new tag by then anyway.

# Florida Dog ID Law: What Your Dog Tag Must Say (and What It Probably Should)

> Florida dog tag rules vary by county. Learn what to engrave, how rabies and license tags fit in, and where to check local requirements. Not legal advice.

Canonical page: https://saltydogtags.com/guides/florida-dog-id-law-tag-requirements/

Salty Dog Tags · Updated Oct 13, 2026

Your dog has slipped the gate. It's 94 degrees, the humidity feels like a wet towel, and somewhere in the neighborhood a very confident animal is investigating a stranger's pool screen. The only thing standing between "fun little adventure" and "three days of panic posting" is a piece of metal about the size of a quarter.

So what does Florida actually require that piece of metal to say?

We make dog tags for a living. We're a bulldog family in Utah that sells to Florida dog people, and we live with seven English bulldogs, which means we have personally tested every escape scenario a short-legged, low-motivation, snack-driven animal can invent. We are not lawyers, though, and Florida is not one big rulebook. It's 67 counties and a long list of cities, each with its own ideas.

Here's the honest version: what's generally true statewide, what's handled locally, how to find your local rules, and what we'd engrave on a tag if it were our dog wandering around Jacksonville.

**Quick disclaimer, said plainly:** This article is general information, not legal advice. Laws and local ordinances change. For the rules that apply to you, check your county animal services office, your city's ordinances, and your veterinarian.

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## The Short Answer: Florida Rules Depend on Where You Live

People usually want one clean sentence like "Florida requires dog tags to say X." It doesn't really work that way.

**The statewide piece:** Florida law requires dogs 4 months and older to be vaccinated against rabies by a licensed veterinarian, with a booster 12 months later and then on the vaccine's schedule ([Fla. Stat. 828.30](https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/828.30)). Your vet gives you a rabies certificate (and usually a tag). That much is consistent across the state. The statute doesn't require the tag to be worn and doesn't set up licensing, and counties and cities can adopt equal or stricter rabies rules.

**The local piece:** A lot of the details are set by counties and cities:

- Whether your dog needs a county or city license (sometimes called registration)
- Whether your dog has to wear the rabies tag or license tag in public
- Leash rules, beach access, park rules, and penalties

Some Florida counties tie licensing directly to rabies vaccination, often through your vet when you get the shot. Others handle it a little differently. A tag rule that applies in one county may not apply across the county line, and city rules can add their own layer.

So the most accurate answer to "what must a Florida dog tag say?" is this: **whatever your county and city require, which usually involves the rabies tag your vet issues and possibly a local license tag.** Your personal ID tag, the one with your phone number, is mostly about getting your dog home quickly.

## Three Different Tags, Three Different Jobs

Dog owners mix these up all the time. On the collar they're all small, jingly, and easy to lose behind the sofa.

### 1. The Rabies Tag

Your veterinarian usually gives you this when your dog is vaccinated. It typically shows a tag number connected to your dog's vaccination record, along with info that identifies the clinic or issuing agency.

Its job is proving your dog is vaccinated, or at least giving someone a way to look it up. If your dog bites someone or ends up at a shelter, that number matters. Whether your dog is required to *wear* it is usually a local question, so check with your county.

### 2. The County or City License Tag

If your area requires a license, you'll typically get a tag with a license number. Some places issue it through your vet, some through animal services, some online. It shows your dog is registered locally, and in many places it also helps animal services contact you.

Fees, renewal schedules, and whether the tag has to be worn all vary. This is the tag people most often don't know they need.

### 3. Your Personal ID Tag

This is the one you design, and the one we make. It has your phone number, your dog's name, and whatever other useful (or unhinged) information you want to add.

As far as we know, Florida doesn't have a statewide rule spelling out the exact wording of a personal ID tag. Even so, it's the tag most likely to get your dog home fast. A neighbor at 9 p.m. can't call the county records office. They can call the number on the tag.

## How to Check Your Local Florida Requirements

Since the rules are local, here's where to look:

- **Your county animal services website.** Search "[your county] animal services dog license" or "[your county] pet licensing." Look for licensing, rabies, and tag sections.
- **Your city's code of ordinances.** If you live inside city limits, your city may have its own animal rules. Most Florida cities post their codes online.
- **Your veterinarian.** Vets in your area deal with local rabies and licensing requirements every day. Ask them directly: "Does my county require a license, and does my dog need to wear the tag?"
- **Call animal services.** It's free, it's quick, and you'll get an answer that applies to your actual address instead of a guess from a forum.

If you move, even just across a county line, check again. Your old county's rules don't come with you.

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## What Your Personal Dog Tag Should Say

The legal tags are about compliance. Your ID tag is about getting your dog back. Here's what we'd put on it, roughly in order of importance.

### Your Phone Number (Non-Negotiable)

This is the most important thing on the tag. If you only have room for one line, it's this one.

- Use a number you actually answer, including from unknown callers.
- Add a second number if you can, like a partner, family member, or trusted neighbor.
- Update the tag when your number changes. A tag with a dead number is jewelry.

### Your Dog's Name (Usually, With a Caveat)

Some people leave the name off, worried that a stranger could use it to lure the dog. Others put it on because it helps calm a scared dog and makes the finder's job easier. Both are reasonable choices. For what it's worth, our bulldogs respond to their names roughly as often as they respond to taxes, so we're not sure either side matters much at our house.

### "Microchipped"

If your dog is chipped, say so. It tells a finder or shelter to scan, and it may make the dog look less like an easy grab for someone with bad intentions. Then make sure the chip is actually **registered with your current contact info.** An unregistered chip is a very small rock.

### Medical Needs

If your dog needs daily medication, has seizures, is diabetic, is deaf, or has a serious allergy, put it on the tag. "Needs meds" fits on almost anything and changes how urgently someone treats a found dog.

### City or Neighborhood (Optional)

A short location line like "Tampa" or "Lives on Elm St" can help, especially for dogs that wander but don't go far. It's optional, and it's your call how much you want to share.

### What You Can Usually Skip

- **Your full street address.** Many people prefer not to engrave it. A phone number does the job.
- **Paragraphs.** It's a tag, not a memoir. Short lines engrave cleaner and read faster.

## The Fun Part: Personality on the Back

Once the useful stuff is covered, there's usually room for character. That's kind of our whole thing.

A good back-of-tag line does two jobs. It makes people laugh, and a laughing stranger is a stranger who's more likely to pick up the phone. It also says something true about your dog. A few from our catalog that fit Florida life a little too well:

- *Can't swim. Still at the beach.*
- *Beach bum. Return to sand.*
- *Lifeguard (off duty).*
- *Not lost. Taking a tour.*
- *Outside is overrated. Take me home.*
- *Built for comfort, not speed.*

And for the bulldog people who already know:

- *I snore. It's not a medical thing.*
- *Snores louder than dad.*
- *Runs on naps and spite.*

Put the jokes on one side and the phone number on the other, so the information doesn't get lost in the comedy.

## Florida-Specific Reasons to Get the Tag Right

Florida has some conditions that make a good ID tag especially worth having:

- **Heat.** A lost dog in Florida summer, especially a flat-faced breed like ours, can get into trouble fast. A tag that gets a phone call in minutes instead of hours matters.
- **Storm season.** Evacuations, shelters, and broken fences are part of Florida life. Dogs get separated in chaos. Keep tags and microchip info current before storm season, not during it.
- **Beaches, parks, and boats.** Dog-friendly beaches and parks often have their own rules, and some may ask about vaccination or licensing. Panama City Beach's official dog beach page, for example, requires dogs to be current on shots and wear ID tags ([pcbfl.gov](https://pcbfl.gov/about-us/visitors/dogs)). Check the specific beach or park before you go.
- **Snowbirds and movers.** If you split time between Florida and somewhere else, use a phone number that works in both places, and check licensing in each.

## A Note on Tag Durability

Florida is hard on metal. Salt air, pool chlorine, sand, and a dog that rolls in everything all wear tags down. Engraving that fades into a smooth blank isn't helping anyone.

Laser engraving holds up better than shallow stamping or printed tags, which is why we use it. Still, check your tags every few months. If you're squinting to read your own phone number, a stranger won't manage it at dusk.

Check with your county, get the rabies tag sorted, and then give your dog an ID tag that's useful and a little bit salty. Seven bulldogs personally vouch for the snack-based recovery method, and you can find the tags at [saltydogtags.com](https://saltydogtags.com/).

*This article is general information, not legal advice, and it is not a substitute for checking official sources. Animal-control laws, leash rules, beach hours, fees and access change, sometimes overnight after storms. Florida's statewide rabies requirement is in Florida Statutes section 828.30. Licensing, tag and leash rules are set by your county and city. Before you rely on anything here, confirm it with your county animal services office, the city, county or state park that runs the beach, and your veterinarian. Salty Dog Tags is not responsible for changes made after publication.*

- [From $12**Build a tag →** — Pick a line or write your own. Name and number go on the back.](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)

## More guides

[Florida dog ID law](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/best-dog-beaches-florida-gulf-coast/) · [What to Put on a Dog Tag](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/what-to-put-on-a-dog-tag/) · [Stainless vs Aluminum vs Brass Dog Tags](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/stainless-vs-aluminum-vs-brass-dog-tags/) · [Tags by breed](https://saltydogtags.com/dog-tags-by-breed/) · [All guides →](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/) · [Build a tag →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)

Questions humans ask

## FAQ

Still stuck? [hello@saltydogtags.com](mailto:hello@saltydogtags.com). A human answers. The dogs supervise.

**Does Florida have one statewide law saying what a dog tag must say?**

Florida requires rabies vaccination for dogs statewide, but licensing and tag-wearing rules are largely set by counties and cities. We're not aware of a statewide rule dictating the wording on a personal ID tag. Check your county animal services and local ordinances for the rules where you live. This isn't legal advice.

**Does my dog have to wear its rabies tag in Florida?**

It depends on your county and city. Some local rules require a rabies or license tag to be worn, and others handle it differently. Your county animal services office or your vet can tell you what applies at your address.

**Is a microchip enough on its own?**

A microchip is great backup, but a finder needs a scanner to read it, usually at a vet or shelter. A visible tag with your phone number can get your dog home without that trip. Use both, and keep the chip registration current.

**Should I put my address on my dog's tag?**

That's up to you. Many owners skip the full address and use one or two reliable phone numbers. A city or neighborhood line is a common middle ground.

**Can I put a funny line on my dog's ID tag?**

Yes. Put your phone number and any key medical info where they're easy to read, then put the personality on the back. A tag that makes someone smile is a tag someone's happy to call.

# 100 Frenchie Names, Grouped by Theme (Because "Potato" Is Taken in Your Group Chat)

> 100 French Bulldog names grouped by theme: pastry, beach, grumpy grandpa, 80s neon and more. Picked by a family living with seven snoring bulldogs.

Canonical page: https://saltydogtags.com/guides/french-bulldog-names/

Salty Dog Tags · Updated Oct 13, 2026

You brought home a French Bulldog. Congratulations. You now own a small, loud, bat-eared loaf that snores like a leaf blower and believes your pillow is community property.

Now it needs a name.

We're a family in Lehi, Utah, with seven English bulldogs. Frenchies are their smaller, pointier-eared cousins who got the same snore in a travel size. We spend our days laser-engraving tags for dogs exactly like yours, so we've seen a lot of names. Some were great. Some were "Dog." We're not here to judge. We're here to help you do better than "Dog."

Below are 100 Frenchie names, grouped by theme. Pick one that fits your dog's personality, or the personality you're hoping they'll grow into. (They won't. But hope is free.)

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## Actually French Names (For the Purists)

Your dog is technically French. Lean in. These names work whether you're in Paris, Pensacola, or a Publix parking lot.

- **Pierre**: Sounds like he owns a vineyard. Owns a chew toy.
- **Margot**: Elegant. Will still eat a sock.
- **Gigi**: Short, sassy, fits on any tag.
- **Remy**: For the Frenchie who's definitely been in the kitchen.
- **Colette**: Classy enough for brunch, wild enough to steal yours.
- **Jacques**: Say it with a shrug.
- **Lulu**: Impossible to yell angrily. That's the point.
- **Bijou**: Means "jewel." Acts like one. Demands to be carried like one.
- **Amélie**: For the whimsical little weirdo.
- **Gaston**: Big personality. Bigger ego. Small legs.

## Pastry and Snack Names (Because Look at Them)

Frenchies are shaped like baked goods. This is not an insult. It's a fact supported by every photo on your phone.

- **Croissant**: Curls up exactly like one.
- **Brioche**: Soft, round, slightly buttery-looking.
- **Crêpe**: Flat. Usually on the couch.
- **Baguette**: Ironic if your dog is a perfect circle.
- **Macaron**: Fancy, colorful, expensive to maintain.
- **Éclair**: Sweet outside, chaos filling.
- **Beignet**: A little French, a little New Orleans, all powdered-sugar energy.
- **Truffle**: Fancy. Also sniffs the ground constantly.
- **Nugget**: The universal small-dog name. Earned its spot.
- **Waffle**: For the Frenchie with wrinkles you could pour syrup into.

## Florida Beach Names (Sun, Sand, and Strategic Shade)

Plenty of our tags end up on dogs living the Florida life. One honest note: Frenchies and heat do not get along. Those squished faces make cooling down hard, so beach days mean early mornings, shade, water, and an air-conditioned retreat. Name them after the beach. Let them enjoy it from under the umbrella.

- **Key Lime**: Tart. Sweet. Very Florida.
- **Mango**: Bright, juicy personality.
- **Sandy**: Will bring the beach home in every wrinkle.
- **Coconut**: Hard to crack. Soft inside.
- **Gator**: Tiny dog, big Florida energy.
- **Pelican**: Will dive for dropped food.
- **Biscayne**: Sounds like a yacht. Is a snorer.
- **Sunny**: For the optimist. Or the one who lies in sunbeams like a lizard.
- **Marlin**: Big fish name for a small dog with big-fish confidence.
- **Flip Flop**: Because that's the sound of them trotting down the hall.

## Tiny Tough Guy Names (Irony Is a Love Language)

There's nothing funnier than a 22-pound dog named after a monster truck. Our English bulldogs back us up here. Nobody takes "Tank" seriously when he's asleep upside down.

- **Tank**: Built like one. Moves like a parked one.
- **Brutus**: Roman emperor energy. Bathtime meltdown energy.
- **Bruiser**: Bruises nothing. Bruised by a falling leaf.
- **Moose**: For the chunky boy.
- **Diesel**: Runs loud. Smells about right.
- **Rocco**: Sounds like he knows a guy.
- **Duke**: Small kingdom. Big attitude.
- **Boss**: He is not the boss. He thinks he is.
- **Rambo**: Afraid of the vacuum.
- **Thor**: God of thunder. Also god of under-the-blanket.

## Old Person Names (Frenchies Are Born Retired)

French Bulldogs come out of the box acting like they've already done 40 years at the plant. Give them a name that matches their aura of a guy complaining about the thermostat.

- **Gerald**: Wants to see a manager.
- **Doris**: Has opinions about your shoes.
- **Walter**: Naps at 2. Naps at 3. Naps at 4.
- **Mildred**: Suspicious of strangers. And friends.
- **Harold**: Groans getting off the couch. Was on the couch for nine minutes.
- **Bernice**: Bridge club president. Treat club treasurer.
- **Frank**: Says exactly what he means. Usually with a snort.
- **Gladys**: Sweet as pie. Will still bite your ankle.
- **Murray**: Retired in Boca. Mentally.
- **Edna**: Strict. Loving. Will not be rushed.

## Bat Ear and Gadget Names (Antennas Not Included)

Those ears pick up the sound of a cheese wrapper from three rooms away. Name them accordingly.

- **Radar**: Hears snacks. Ignores "come here."
- **Yoda**: The resemblance is uncanny. You know it.
- **Gremlin**: Do not feed after midnight. Or before. They'll lie about it.
- **Dobby**: Free. Spoiled. Won't give the sock back.
- **Gizmo**: Cute until something gets wet.
- **Mothman**: For the Frenchie who appears silently at the foot of the bed at 3 a.m.
- **Sonar**: Echolocates the fridge.
- **Echo**: Repeats every bark twice, for emphasis.
- **Satellite**: Two dishes on top, full coverage.
- **Bluetooth**: Pairs with your lap automatically.

## Snort and Sound Effect Names (Say It How They Sound)

Anyone who lives with a flat-faced dog knows the soundtrack: snorts, wheezes, honks, and noises you can't explain to houseguests. We live with seven of these soundtracks. Trust us.

- **Oink**: The first noise you heard. The last noise you'll hear tonight.
- **Piglet**: Same energy, more Hundred Acre Wood.
- **Wheezy**: Affectionate. Accurate.
- **Tuba**: Low brass snoring section.
- **Rumble**: For the dog whose snore rattles the windows.
- **Snuffles**: Classic. Sniffs everything twice.
- **Hiccup**: Small, sudden, a little dramatic.
- **Tooter**: You already know. Everyone in the room already knows.
- **Grunt**: The noise they make when asked to move.
- **Honk**: Sounds like a goose. Lives like a king.

## Fancy and Bougie Names (For the Pampered Loaf)

Some Frenchies ride in strollers. Some have more sweaters than you. These names are for them.

- **Duchess**: Will not walk on wet grass.
- **Winston**: Every bulldog family knows a Winston. He's always the boss of the couch.
- **Chanel**: Smells nothing like it.
- **Dior**: High fashion. Low ground clearance.
- **Monsieur**: Insist that the vet uses it.
- **Baron**: Lord of the dog bed.
- **Vivienne**: Glamorous. Snores like a trucker.
- **Reginald**: Reggie for short, Reginald when he's in trouble.
- **Countess**: Counts treats. Notices if one is missing.
- **Bentley**: Luxury model. Expensive repairs.

## 80s Synthwave Names (Our Personal Favorites)

Our whole brand runs on neon, sunsets, and cassette-tape energy, so of course this section exists. Bonus points if your dog wears sunglasses at night.

- **Neon**: Bright personality, glows in the dark (spiritually).
- **Miami**: Florida icon. Pastel suit not required.
- **Vice**: Pairs nicely with Miami if you've got two.
- **Turbo**: For the Frenchie zoomies, which last about 40 feet.
- **Laser**: We engrave with them. We're biased.
- **Cassette**: Rewinds the same bad behavior on repeat.
- **Ferris**: Takes a day off. Every day.
- **Maverick**: Feels the need. The need for snacks.
- **Blondie**: For the fawn or cream Frenchie with rock star energy.
- **Nova**: Cosmic, short, fits beautifully on a tag.

## Salty Attitude Names (For the Dogs Who Earned It)

Some dogs are sweethearts. Some are menaces in a cute costume. These names are honest.

- **Chaos**: Self-explanatory.
- **Menace**: Certified. Laminated.
- **Havoc**: Wreaks it, daily, before breakfast.
- **Spite**: Runs on naps and this.
- **Trouble**: You were warned. You said yes anyway.
- **Riot**: Small dog. Big mouth.
- **Mayhem**: Your throw pillows already know.
- **Bandit**: Steals food, socks, and hearts, in that order.
- **Rascal**: Grandma-approved menace.
- **Pepper**: Little, spicy, gets in everything.

## How to Pick the Right Name (From People Who Engrave Them for a Living)

A few practical tips from the engraving bench:

- **Shorter names read better on tags.** "Gigi" fits big and bold. "Sir Reginald Waffleton III" fits too, but in very small letters. Your call.
- **Say it out loud, angrily, in public.** You will yell this name at a dog park. Make sure you're okay with strangers hearing "TOOTER, NO."
- **Avoid names that sound like commands.** "Kit" sounds like "sit." "Bo" sounds like "no." Your dog will be confused, though honestly, they were going to ignore you anyway.
- **Give it a week.** Sometimes a dog grows into a name. Sometimes they make it obvious you got it wrong.

Once you've got a name, pair it with a line that fits. Our [Frenchie tags page](https://saltydogtags.com/frenchie-dog-tags/) has plenty for flat-faced dogs, and so does the [bulldog page](https://saltydogtags.com/bulldog-dog-tags/): "Snorts. Means it." "Built for comfort, not speed." "Velcro dog. Will not detach." The saying goes on the front; name and phone number go on the back. More on that in [what to put on a dog tag](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/what-to-put-on-a-dog-tag/), and if you also have a big cousin at home, see [bulldog names](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/bulldog-names/).

Found the perfect name? Put it on something that'll survive the dog park, the beach, and a Frenchie who rolls in everything. Our laser-engraved tags, built in [the builder](https://saltydogtags.com/#build), are made by a family that knows the snore personally.

Questions humans ask

## FAQ

Still stuck? [hello@saltydogtags.com](mailto:hello@saltydogtags.com). A human answers. The dogs supervise.

**What's a good name for a French Bulldog?**

The best name fits your dog's personality. Grumpy loafs suit old-person names like Gerald or Edna. Wild ones suit Chaos or Riot. Round ones suit pastries. If you're stuck, watch your dog for a few days. They'll show you who they are, usually by destroying something.

**Should I give my Frenchie a French name?**

You can, and names like Pierre, Margot, and Bijou are a fun nod to the breed. But no rule says you have to. Plenty of great Frenchies are named Tank, Mango, or Doris. Your dog does not care where the name comes from. Your dog cares if the name sounds like "treat."

**Are short names better for dogs?**

Generally, yes. One- or two-syllable names are easier to call out and easier for dogs to pick up. They also engrave larger and cleaner on a tag, which matters when someone's squinting at your dog's collar while they wiggle.

**What should I put on my Frenchie's dog tag?**

At minimum: your dog's name and a phone number that you actually answer. Many people add "Microchipped" or a note about medical needs. After that, there's room for personality. A funny line on a tag doesn't replace the important info, but it does make the stranger who finds your dog smile while they dial.

**Do Frenchies do okay in Florida?**

They can live happily in Florida with smart care, but their short snouts make heat and humidity genuinely risky. Walk early or late, keep them in shade and air conditioning, always bring water, and skip midday beach trips. Name them Key Lime. Keep them cool.
