# Gifts for Bulldog Owners: Ideas From a House With Seven of Them

> Gift ideas for bulldog owners from a family with seven English bulldogs: cooling gear, wrinkle care, snore survival, and funny engraved tags.

Canonical page: https://saltydogtags.com/guides/gifts-for-bulldog-owners/

Salty Dog Tags · Updated Oct 12, 2026

Buying a gift for a bulldog owner is easy. Buying one they'll actually use is harder.

Bulldog people don't need another mug that says "Dog Mom" in a font that looks like it was rescued from a scrapbook. They need things that survive drool, heat, snoring, and a 50-pound potato who considers furniture a personal right.

We live with seven English bulldogs in Lehi, Utah. Seven. On purpose. So we've tested a lot of bulldog stuff the hard way: by buying it, watching a bulldog destroy or ignore it, and buying something else. This guide is what survived.

Whether your bulldog person is sweating it out in Florida humidity or dealing with dry mountain summers, here's what to get them.

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## Start With the Truth: Bulldogs Are a Lifestyle, Not a Pet

Before you shop, understand who you're buying for. A bulldog owner:

- Has accepted that they'll never sleep in silence again.
- Owns more towels than any reasonable adult should.
- Checks the weather forecast for the dog before checking it for themselves.
- Has cleaned a face wrinkle and felt something like spiritual growth.

The best gifts make one of those realities easier, funnier, or both. Ideally both.

## Cooling Gear (Especially for Florida Bulldog Families)

Bulldogs and heat aren't friends. Their short snouts make it harder for them to cool down, so anything that helps keep a bulldog comfortable in warm weather is a gift the owner will genuinely appreciate.

**Good options:**

- **A cooling mat.** Pressure-activated gel mats or elevated mesh cots that let air flow underneath. Our dogs claim these like it's prime real estate. If you're shopping for someone in Florida, this belongs near the top of the list.
- **A cooling vest or bandana.** You soak it, wring it out, and put it on the dog. It looks slightly ridiculous. Bulldogs are used to that.
- **A quiet floor fan.** Not glamorous. Extremely practical. Bonus points if it's sturdy enough to survive a curious bulldog nose.
- **A portable water bottle with a built-in bowl.** For walks, beach trips, and the inevitable moment the dog sits down mid-walk and refuses to continue.

A quick note: cooling gear helps, but it doesn't replace common sense. Short walks, shade, early mornings, and air conditioning are still the plan. Any responsible bulldog owner already knows this. Your gift just makes it a little easier.

## Wrinkle and Skin Care Supplies

If you've never cleaned a bulldog's face folds, congratulations on your peaceful life. For everyone else, wrinkle care is a regular chore, and it's a real part of keeping these dogs comfortable.

**Gift ideas that get used:**

- **Pet-safe wrinkle wipes.** Unscented, gentle, and bought in quantities that would alarm a normal person.
- **A wrinkle balm or paste.** Ask the owner what their vet recommends, or pick up the brand they already use. Bulldog people have opinions about this. Respect them.
- **Soft microfiber cloths.** For drying folds after cleaning, because damp wrinkles are trouble.
- **Paw balm.** For cracked pads from hot pavement, sand, or general bulldog living.
- **Tear stain wipes.** Some bulldogs get them. Their owners will thank you quietly and sincerely.

Put a few of these together in a basket and you've got a "Wrinkle Maintenance Kit." It's unglamorous and it's thoughtful, and that combination works on bulldog people every time.

## Beds That Respect the Bulldog Lifestyle

Bulldogs sleep a lot. They're very good at it. A good bed is a gift for both the dog and the human who would like their couch back.

**Look for:**

- **Orthopedic or memory foam beds.** Bulldogs are stocky, heavy for their size, and prone to joint issues as they age. Supportive foam makes sense.
- **Bolster beds.** Bulldogs love a headrest. They'll drape their face over the edge like a tiny, snoring Roman emperor.
- **Removable, machine-washable covers.** Non-negotiable. Drool happens. Toots happen. Everything gets washed.
- **Low entry height.** Bulldogs aren't built for jumping, and they know it.

Skip anything delicate, decorative, or "dry clean only." That's not a dog bed. That's a future crime scene.

## Snore Survival Gifts (For the Humans)

Here's the gift category nobody talks about: things for the *owner* to survive the dog.

Bulldogs snore. Ours snore in harmony, which is impressive and also unbearable. Gifts that acknowledge this reality land well:

- **A white noise machine.** Fight snoring with a more pleasant noise.
- **Good earplugs.** Practical. Slightly passive-aggressive. Perfect.
- **A heavy-duty lint roller set.** Bulldog fur is short, stiff, and weaves itself into fabric like it pays rent.
- **A cordless handheld vacuum.** For fur, crumbs, and whatever the dog dragged in from the yard.
- **A stack of cheap, absorbent towels.** Drool towels. Bath towels. "Why is the floor wet" towels. A bulldog home can always use more.

These aren't flashy, but bulldog owners will use them daily. Which is more than you can say for a candle shaped like a paw.

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## A Custom Engraved Dog Tag With Actual Personality

Every dog needs an ID tag. Most of them are boring. Name, phone number, done. That's the dog equivalent of a plain white T-shirt.

A custom engraved tag is a useful gift that also shows you understand the dog's personality. And every bulldog has a personality, mostly a confident one with a short list of priorities.

At Salty Dog Tags, we laser-engrave funny dog tags with a setup and a punchline. Short, dry, honest. A few that tend to fit bulldogs a little too well (the full set is on our [bulldog tags page](https://saltydogtags.com/bulldog-dog-tags/)):

- *"I snore. It's not a medical thing."*
- *"Runs on naps and spite."*
- *"Built for comfort, not speed."*
- *"Snores louder than dad."*
- *"Can't swim. Still at the beach."* (A strong pick for Florida bulldog families.)
- *"Snorts. Means it."*

The back of the tag still carries what matters: the phone number and contact info that gets the dog home. The front just tells the world what the family already knows.

**Tips for gifting a tag:**

- **Get the right contact info.** If it's a surprise, quietly confirm the phone number they want on it. A tag with the wrong number is just jewelry.
- **Match the line to the dog.** The couch-dweller gets "Professional snuggler." The escape artist gets "Not lost. Taking a tour." The chaos gremlin gets "Certified menace."
- **Know your audience.** We have an adults-only collection with lines that'd make your grandmother clutch her pearls. Great for the right friend. Maybe not for the office gift exchange.

Pair a tag with a sturdy harness (more on that next) and you've got a gift that's practical, personal, and funny.

## Harnesses, Leashes, and Gear Built for a Tank

Bulldogs have thick necks, broad chests, and the pulling power of a small tractor when they spot something interesting. Many owners prefer a harness over walking on a collar alone, because it spreads pressure across the chest instead of the throat.

**Gift ideas:**

- **A well-fitted harness.** Front-clip or back-clip styles made for broad, stocky breeds. Check the sizing chart carefully. Bulldog sizing is its own math.
- **A padded leash.** Easier on the hands when the dog decides to plant itself and refuse to move. Which it will.
- **A wide, comfortable collar** to hold that engraved tag. The collar carries ID. The harness handles the walking.
- **A car seat cover or hammock.** Bulldogs love car rides and hate keeping their drool to themselves.

## Toys That Survive Bulldog Jaws

Bulldogs aren't always aggressive chewers, but many are thorough ones. Pick toys accordingly.

- **Durable rubber chew toys** sized appropriately so they can't be swallowed.
- **Treat-dispensing puzzle toys** for the bulldog who's too smart for its own good, which is most of them, at least when food is involved.
- **Sturdy tug toys** for low-key indoor play.
- **Lick mats** for a slower, calmer snack session.

Avoid anything small enough to be inhaled. Bulldogs approach food and toys with the same energy: enthusiasm first, consequences later.

## Sentimental and Just-for-Fun Gifts

Sometimes the best gift is the one that makes the owner laugh, or makes them a little misty about their ridiculous wrinkly roommate.

- **A custom pet portrait.** Classic oil-painting style, cartoon style, or 80s synthwave neon, if you want to match our energy.
- **A photo book** of the dog's greatest moments, which are mostly naps.
- **A bulldog-themed hoodie or tee** with a line they'd actually say out loud.
- **A framed paw print** made with a pet-safe ink kit.
- **A matching engraved tag** for each dog in a multi-bulldog household. Trust us, nobody stops at one bulldog. We certainly didn't.

## How to Pick the Right Gift

Still stuck? Ask yourself:

- **Where do they live?** Hot and humid, like most of Florida? Lean into cooling gear. Dry, high-altitude summers? Paw balm and water bottles.
- **How old is the dog?** Puppies need toys and patience. Seniors need orthopedic beds and gentle care.
- **What's the owner's sense of humor?** Dry and salty? Get the funny tag. Sweet and sentimental? Go for the portrait. Both? Do both.
- **What do they complain about most?** Snoring, fur, drool, or heat. Solve that problem and you're a hero.

Shopping for a bulldog person? Find a tag that says what their dog is thinking, laser-engraved by a family that's outnumbered seven to one, in [the builder](https://saltydogtags.com/#build), or start with our [bulldog sayings](https://saltydogtags.com/bulldog-dog-tags/).

- [From $12**Build a tag →** — Pick a line or write your own. Name and number go on the back.](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)

Questions humans ask

## FAQ

Still stuck? [hello@saltydogtags.com](mailto:hello@saltydogtags.com). A human answers. The dogs supervise.

**What's the best gift for a new bulldog owner?**

A practical starter bundle works well: wrinkle wipes, a washable bed, a well-fitted harness, and an engraved ID tag with their contact info. New owners are still figuring things out, and anything that covers basic care is genuinely helpful.

**Are cooling mats worth it for bulldogs?**

For many bulldogs, yes, especially in hot climates like Florida. Bulldogs can struggle with heat, and a cooling mat gives them a comfortable spot to rest. It's a helpful tool alongside shade, AC, and short walks during the cooler parts of the day, not a replacement for them.

**Should a bulldog wear a collar or a harness?**

Many bulldog owners use both: a collar to carry the ID tag and a harness for walks. A harness spreads pressure across the chest, which a lot of owners prefer for short-snouted breeds. When in doubt, the owner's vet is the right person to ask.

**What should go on a custom dog tag?**

At minimum, a reliable phone number. Many people add the dog's name and a backup contact. After that, it's your call. Our tags put a funny line on the front so the dog can introduce itself with some attitude.

**Are your funny tags appropriate for kids?**

Most of our catalog is family-friendly, covering snoring, snacks, and general menace behavior. We also have a clearly labeled adults-only collection for people with a saltier sense of humor. Pick accordingly.

# St. George Dog License Rules (Plus Washington City, Hurricane and Ivins)

> St. George dog license fees, deadlines and the two-dog rule, plus Washington City, Hurricane and Ivins, from the city pages. And how an ID tag differs.

Canonical page: https://saltydogtags.com/guides/st-george-dog-license-rules/

Salty Dog Tags · Updated Nov 16, 2026

A dog's collar in Washington County usually carries two pieces of metal with two different jobs. The **license tag** comes from your city and shows your dog is licensed. The **ID tag** is the one you buy, with your phone number on it, so whoever finds your dog can call you instead of the shelter. We make the second kind. The first kind is a city matter, so everything below comes straight from official city pages, linked, as checked on 2026-11-16.

Rules really do differ city by city here. St. George renews every year, Washington City every two years, and Ivins until the rabies certificate runs out. Find your city below, or call your animal control office if it isn't listed.

| City | Who needs one | How long it lasts | Fee per dog | Bring

| **[St. George](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/st-george-dog-license-rules/#st-george)** | Dogs 4 months and older; a new dog within 10 days | January 1 to December 31; renew by February 28 | $10 spayed or neutered, $20 not | Proof of rabies vaccination

| **[Washington City](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/st-george-dog-license-rules/#washington-city)** | All dogs; part-time residents after 30 days | Two years | $20 altered, $40 not altered | Current proof of rabies

| **[Hurricane](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/st-george-dog-license-rules/#hurricane)** | Dogs by 4 months; a new dog within 30 days | Due January 1 | $10 spayed or neutered, $25 not | Current rabies certificate

| **[Ivins](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/st-george-dog-license-rules/#ivins-and-santa-clara)** | Dogs licensed with Ivins City | Until the rabies certificate expires | $5 a year altered, $10 unaltered | Current rabies certificate

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## St. George

- Dogs **4 months or older** must be licensed by the city, and a dog you get during the year needs a license **within 10 days**.
- Fees per dog: **$10** if spayed or neutered, **$20** if not.
- Tags go on sale **January 1** and expire **December 31**. Renewals are due by **February 28**. After that the late fee is **$5 per month per dog**, up to $20 per dog.
- **Only two dogs per residence** are permitted in St. George, the city's licensing page says.
- Just visiting? Temporary-resident dogs with a current license tag from another city or county don't need a St. George license.
- Apply online or with the fillable PDF on the city page. The online form asks for **proof of rabies vaccination** and, if it applies, a spay or neuter certificate. Owners of unlicensed dogs can be cited and fined.
- **St. George Animal Shelter:** 605 E Waterworks Rd, 435-627-4350. By appointment only, Monday to Saturday; closed Sunday.

Sources: [City of St. George dog licensing](https://sgcityutah.gov/doglicense/) and [St. George Animal Services and Shelter](https://www.sgcityutah.gov/departments/police_department/animal_services___shelter.php).

## Washington City

- **All dogs** in the city must be licensed, and a license is **valid for two years**.
- You need **current proof of rabies** to license. Spayed or neutered pets get a discount.
- Part-time residents who are in the city **longer than 30 days** must license their dogs.
- The city's fee schedule lists a two-year license at **$20 altered** or **$40 not altered**, **$50** for a third dog, **$75** for a fourth dog, a **$120** lifetime license and **$5** for a replacement tag.
- If your dog is picked up wandering, the impound fee is **$50** for a first offense plus **$10 per day**.
- Apply online from the city page. **Washington City Animal Shelter:** 95 E Industrial Dr., (435) 673-7194. Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.; closed weekends and holidays.

Sources: [Washington City Animal Welfare Services](https://washingtonutah.gov/services/publicsafety/police/animalwelfare) and the [Washington City Master Fee Schedule](https://washingtonutah.gov/government/budget/MasterFeeSchedule/&key=7).

## Hurricane

- City ordinance: your dog must be licensed **by 4 months of age**, and a new dog **within 30 days** of getting it.
- Each residential address may license **up to four dogs** per calendar year.
- **A license and rabies tag must be attached to your dog's collar.** Hurricane is the one city here that says so on its page.
- Bring proof of a **current rabies vaccination**: a current certificate from your vet. Online, a photo of the rabies tag is not accepted.
- Fees: **$10** spayed or neutered, **$25** not. When we checked, the page said licenses were due January 1, 2026 and fees go up by $20 per residence from March 1, 2026. Check the page for next year's dates.
- Buy a license at the animal shelter, at the Police Department (90 S 700 W, cash or check), online, or at Desert Vet and Zion Vet between December and February.
- **Hurricane Animal Shelter:** 2084 S 700 W, 435-635-8314.

Source: [Hurricane City Animal Control and Shelter](https://www.cityofhurricane.com/159/Animal-Control-Shelter).

## Ivins and Santa Clara

Ivins and Santa Clara share the Santa Clara–Ivins Public Safety Department, which handles animal problems for both cities. Its **animal control office** is at 474 N 200 W, Ivins, 435-628-1049.

- **Ivins:** the city's dog license application lists **$5 per dog per year** for an altered dog and **$10** for an unaltered dog. A **current rabies certificate** is required, and the license is **valid until the rabies certificate expires** (you can pick a shorter term). The form lists Ivins City at 85 N. Main St., 435-628-0606.
- **Santa Clara:** we couldn't find Santa Clara's own license fees or rules on an official page, so we're not going to guess. Call Santa Clara–Ivins animal control.

Sources: [Ivins dog license application (IC Form 3002)](https://ivinsutah.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Dog-License-Application-IC-Form-3002-2024-05-10.pdf), [Ivins animal shelter and control](https://ivinsutah.gov/document-category/animal-shelter-control/) and [Santa Clara–Ivins Public Safety](https://ivinsutah.gov/public-safety-3/).

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## New to Washington County?

The deadlines start the day the dog (or you) arrives:

- **St. George:** a dog you get during the year needs a license within 10 days. Visiting dogs with a current tag from elsewhere don't need one.
- **Washington City:** part-time residents who stay longer than 30 days must license their dogs.
- **Hurricane:** a new dog needs a license within 30 days.

## What goes on the collar

None of these pages dictate what your personal ID tag has to say. They issue the license tag, and the rest is up to you. Our advice, from a house where every bulldog has tested the fence at least once:

- **The license tag** from your city, so animal control can look your dog up.
- **The rabies tag**, if your vet gave you one. In Hurricane, the license and rabies tag are required on the collar.
- **An ID tag with your phone number**, big and readable. A license number means a call to an office during office hours. Your number means a call to you, right now.

**To be clear: our tags are ID tags, not license or rabies tags, and they don't satisfy any licensing requirement.** You still need the license from your city.

That third tag is where we come in: name and phone number engraved on the back, something funny on the front. ## FAQ

Still stuck? [hello@saltydogtags.com](mailto:hello@saltydogtags.com). A human answers. The dogs supervise.

**How much is a dog license in St. George, Utah?**

The City of St. George charges $10 per dog if spayed or neutered and $20 if not. Tags go on sale January 1 and expire December 31. Renewals are due by February 28, with a $5 per month late fee per dog after that, up to $20.

**At what age does a dog need a license in St. George?**

Dogs 4 months or older must be licensed by the city, and a dog you get during the year has to be licensed within 10 days. The online form asks for proof of rabies vaccination.

**How many dogs can I have in St. George?**

The city's dog licensing page says only two dogs per residence are permitted in St. George. Hurricane allows up to four licensed dogs per residential address. Other cities set their own limits, so check yours.

**How long does a Washington City dog license last?**

Two years. Washington City requires all dogs in the city to be licensed, with current proof of rabies, and its fee schedule lists $20 for an altered dog and $40 for an unaltered dog for two years.

**Does a Salty Dog Tag count as my dog license?**

No. Our tags are ID tags, not license or rabies tags, and they don't satisfy any licensing requirement. Your license tag comes from your city.

# St. George Dog Parks and Dog-Friendly Trails (With the Leash Rules)

> Fenced dog parks in St. George, Washington City and Hurricane, plus the leash rules for Snow Canyon, Red Cliffs and Zion, from the official pages.

Canonical page: https://saltydogtags.com/guides/st-george-dog-parks-and-trails/

Salty Dog Tags · Updated Nov 16, 2026

St. George dogs get red rock, a lot of sun and some firm leash rules, because Snow Canyon and the Red Cliffs Desert Reserve protect Mojave desert tortoise habitat. Everything below comes from city, state, reserve and National Park Service pages, linked, as checked on 2026-11-16. Directory sites list more parks than this; we only kept the ones an official page confirms.

Bring a leash everywhere. Every set of rules on this page wants it on at the gate or the trailhead.

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## St. George city dog parks

The City of St. George lists three parks with a dog park:

- **Firehouse Park**, 1929 West 1800 North. A 4-acre neighborhood park, and the dog park is a secure fenced area for off-leash play. Drinking fountains, restrooms and parking.
- **J.C. Snow Park**, 275 East 900 South. A 12-acre community park with a dog park, restrooms, drinking fountains and the trailhead for the Hilton Dr. Trail.
- **Riverbend Park**, 810 W. Las Colinas. A fully fenced dog park, a restroom, a drinking fountain, parking and a connection to the trail system.

Each of those pages links the city's dog park rules brochure (the brochure itself is dated 2016). It says:

- Dogs must be **at least 4 months old, fully vaccinated and currently licensed**.
- Dogs must be **leashed when entering and leaving**. Inside, owners stay in the park, in view of their dogs, with the dogs under voice control.
- **No spike collars.** Aggressive dogs and female dogs in heat are not allowed in.
- No food or glass bottles. Scoop the poop, seal it in a bag, and fill any holes your dog digs.
- Children 15 and under must be actively supervised by an adult. **The park closes at 10 p.m.**

For the rest of the city's parks, the Parks page links the park ordinance (City Code Title 7, Chapter 3). The code site wouldn't load for us, so we're not quoting it. Read it before you unclip anywhere that isn't a fenced dog park.

Sources: [Firehouse Park](https://sgcityutah.gov/business_detail_T18_R54.php), [J.C. Snow Park](https://sgcityutah.gov/business_detail_T18_R58.php), [Riverbend Park](https://sgcityutah.gov/business_detail_T18_R582.php), [dog park rules brochure](https://sgcityutah.gov/Documents/Activity%20Events/Parks%20Trails/updateddogparkbrochure.pdf) and [St. George Parks and Trails](https://sgcityutah.gov/parksandrec/parks_andtrails/index.php).

## Washington City

- **Dog Town Dog Park**, 450 South 200 East. Off-leash within the fenced areas, with one area for dogs **under 25 pounds** and one for dogs **over 25 pounds**, plus a water feature for dogs to play in and cool off. Restrooms, a pavilion, a playground, benches and picnic sites.
- In Washington City's other parks, the posted park rules say **pets must be on a 6-foot leash** and the owner is responsible for waste. City parks are open **6 a.m. to 10 p.m.**

Sources: [Dog Town Dog Park](https://washingtonutah.gov/recreation/parks/DogTownDogPark) and [Washington City parks](https://washingtonutah.gov/recreation/parks).

## Hurricane

Hurricane City lists a dog park with **active and passive run areas**, a natural habitat area, parking, pavilions, benches and a perimeter fence. The city says the fencing is installed, the park is open to the public for **limited use**, and it's still taking donations to finish the park. The page gives no street address, so start from the city's facility page.

Source: [Hurricane City dog park](https://www.cityofhurricane.com/Facilities/Facility/Details/Dog-Park-4).

## Ivins and Santa Clara

We didn't find an official Ivins or Santa Clara page for a dog park, so we're leaving them off rather than repeating directory listings. The [Santa Clara–Ivins Public Safety Department](https://ivinsutah.gov/public-safety-3/) handles animal control for both cities and can tell you where dogs can run.

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## Snow Canyon State Park

- **Dogs are permitted on all park trails and in the campground.** At all times they must be leashed (**6 feet max**), under their owner's control, on designated mapped trails, with all waste scooped, bagged and thrown away.
- Why so strict: Snow Canyon is part of the Red Cliffs Desert Reserve, a conservation area for Mojave desert tortoises. The park says tortoises can't tell a dog from a coyote, and that two types of rattlesnakes, Gila monsters, scorpions and spiders live in the canyon. The park's words: an off-leash dog has a much higher chance of coming nose to nose with a venomous animal.
- **Johnson Canyon is closed March 15 through September 14**, except for ranger-guided hikes.
- Summer: the park says daytime temperatures in July and August frequently top 105 degrees. Read our [desert heat guide](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/desert-heat-dog-safety-st-george/) before a summer hike.

Sources: [Snow Canyon State Park](https://stateparks.utah.gov/parks/snow-canyon/) (the questions section) and [current conditions](https://stateparks.utah.gov/parks/snow-canyon/current-conditions/).

## Red Cliffs Desert Reserve

- **All pets must be on a leash**, to prevent wildlife disturbance and to avoid conflicts with other people. Officers patrol the reserve and may issue citations.
- Desert tortoises are protected by federal law, and it's illegal for pets, like people, to harass or harm them. The reserve also warns that rattlesnakes and Gila monsters may bite a pet in self-defense.
- In the reserve's Lowland Zone, travel is restricted to designated trails.
- The one exception: hunting dogs may travel off-leash with a licensed hunter in the act of hunting during official hunting seasons.

Source: [Red Cliffs Desert Reserve rules and regulations](https://www.redcliffsdesertreserve.com/rules).

## Zion National Park

- **The only trail that allows pets is the Pa'rus Trail**, which starts at the Zion Canyon Visitor Center.
- Leashed pets are welcome along public roads and parking areas, in developed campgrounds and picnic areas, and on the Zion Lodge grounds. They are not allowed on any other trail, in wilderness areas, on shuttle buses or in public buildings.
- The leash can be no longer than **6 feet**, and retractable leashes that extend further than 6 feet are not allowed.
- **Keep dogs out of the water.** The park monitors the Virgin River for toxic cyanobacteria, and dogs may ingest cyanobacteria or untreated water.
- Don't leave a pet in the car; the park says Zion is hot and a vehicle can quickly warm to dangerous levels for most of the year. It lists boarding kennels in Hurricane, St. George, Kanab, Cedar City and Rockville.

Source: [Zion National Park: pets](https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/pets.htm).

## Before you go

- **A 6-foot leash** meets every leash rule on this page. Bring bags and water for the dog.
- **Check the collar:** a current license tag, the rabies tag, and an ID tag with a phone number a stranger can read. If your dog slips the leash on a trail, the number is how you get the call.
- **Summer:** go early, and do the pavement test from our [heat guide](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/desert-heat-dog-safety-st-george/) before you leave the parking lot.

Licensing first? Our [St. George license rules guide](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/st-george-dog-license-rules/) has the fees for St. George, Washington City, Hurricane and Ivins. Then [build a tag](https://saltydogtags.com/#build) for the trail.

**Where are the dog parks in St. George?**

The city lists fenced dog parks at Firehouse Park (1929 West 1800 North), J.C. Snow Park (275 East 900 South) and Riverbend Park (810 W. Las Colinas). Washington City has Dog Town Dog Park at 450 South 200 East.

**Are dogs allowed in Snow Canyon State Park?**

Yes. Utah State Parks says dogs are permitted on all park trails and in the campground, on a leash 6 feet or shorter, under control, on designated mapped trails, with waste bagged and binned.

**Which trails in Zion allow dogs?**

Only the Pa'rus Trail, which starts at the Zion Canyon Visitor Center. Pets must be on a leash no longer than 6 feet and are not allowed on other trails, in wilderness areas, on shuttle buses or in public buildings.

The rules brochure the city links from its dog park pages says dogs must be at least 4 months old, fully vaccinated and currently licensed, leashed when entering and leaving, and under voice control. The park closes at 10 p.m.

# Stainless vs Aluminum vs Brass Dog Tags: An Honest Guide From a House With Seven Bulldogs

> Stainless, aluminum, or brass? A salty, honest guide to dog tag metals: durability, weight, engraving, and which survives Florida salt air and slobber.

Canonical page: https://saltydogtags.com/guides/stainless-vs-aluminum-vs-brass-dog-tags/

Salty Dog Tags · Updated Oct 12, 2026

Picking a dog tag seems easy until you're staring at three metals that all look shiny in the product photo. Then the questions start. Which one lasts? Which one is too heavy for a small dog? Which one turns weird colors after a summer in Florida?

We have opinions. We live with seven English bulldogs in Lehi, Utah, which means our tags get dragged across concrete, dunked in water bowls, buried in neck wrinkles, and coated in a level of drool that should probably be studied. A tag that survives our house has earned its keep.

Here's the no-nonsense breakdown of stainless steel, aluminum, and brass: what each is good at, where each falls short, and which one fits your dog's lifestyle. That lifestyle might be "beach bum." It might be "professional snuggler." Either way, there's a metal for that.

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## Why the Metal Matters More Than You Think

A dog tag has one job: get your dog home if they wander off. That's it. It doesn't need to be fancy. It does need to stay readable.

The metal decides how long your phone number stays legible, how much the tag weighs on your dog's collar, and how it handles water, salt, sweat, and the general chaos of being worn by an animal that rolls in things on purpose. It also affects how the engraving looks. Laser engraving interacts differently with each metal, so the same design can look crisp on one and so-so on another.

A tag that reads "Microchipped. Still dumb." is only funny if someone can actually read it.

## Stainless Steel Dog Tags: The Bulldog of Metals

Stainless steel is tough and stubborn, and it doesn't care about your feelings. If metals were dog breeds, stainless would be snoring on the couch while everything around it falls apart.

### The good

- **Durability.** Stainless resists scratches and dents better than aluminum or brass. Your dog can drag it along the sidewalk, chew on it, or bang it against every metal food bowl in the house, and it keeps going.
- **Corrosion resistance.** Stainless is built to resist rust. That makes it a strong pick for dogs who live near the ocean, swim in pools, or drool enough to qualify as a water feature. Some grades, often called "marine grade," handle salt exposure especially well.
- **Engraving that lasts.** Laser engraving on stainless typically produces a dark, permanent mark that sits in the metal rather than on top of it. It won't peel off like paint.
- **Low maintenance.** Rinse it off now and then. That's the whole care routine.

### The not-so-good

- **Weight.** Stainless is heavier than aluminum. On a bulldog, a lab, or any dog built like a coffee table, you won't notice. On a tiny dog, a big stainless tag can feel like jewelry from a bad decision.
- **Noise.** Stainless jingles. Two stainless tags clanking together at 3 a.m. while your dog scratches is a sound you will come to know intimately.
- **Price.** It usually costs a little more than aluminum. Worth it for most dogs, but it's real.

### Best for

Medium and large dogs, water dogs, beach dogs, heavy chewers, and anyone who wants to buy a tag once and forget about it. Whisky, the first of our seven bulldogs to get a tag, wears polished stainless. Seven bulldogs don't leave room for fragile.

## Aluminum Dog Tags: Light, Colorful, and a Little Soft

Aluminum is the lightweight option. It's the tag you pick when you want fun colors and your dog weighs about as much as a bag of flour.

### The good

- **Lightweight.** This is aluminum's biggest selling point. For toy breeds, puppies, cats, and small dogs ("Small dog. Big mouth."), a light tag doesn't drag on the collar or bounce against their chest all day.
- **Color options.** Aluminum tags are often anodized, which adds a colored surface layer. That's how you get the bright pinks, blues, purples, and neon shades. If you're into an 80s synthwave look (we may be biased), aluminum delivers.
- **Sharp engraving contrast.** On anodized aluminum, the laser removes the colored layer and exposes the bright metal underneath. The result is clean, high-contrast text that's easy to read.
- **Budget-friendly.** Aluminum tags are usually the most affordable option.

### The not-so-good

- **Softer metal.** Aluminum scratches and bends more easily than stainless. A dedicated chewer can mangle it.
- **Wear over time.** Heavy rubbing and scraping can scuff the anodized color around the letters, so the tag looks worn sooner than stainless. Laser-engraved letters are bright bare metal, so they stay readable, but tags that clank against other tags or get dragged on the ground show it faster.
- **Not ideal for constant salt exposure.** Aluminum doesn't rust the way plain steel does, but repeated salt water and harsh conditions can still dull or pit the surface over time. A daily Gulf Coast swimmer will put it through a lot.

### Best for

Small dogs, cats, puppies who'll outgrow their collar anyway, indoor pets, and owners who want color and are fine replacing a tag down the road. If your dog's motto is "Outside is overrated. Take me home," aluminum will probably hold up just fine.

## Brass Dog Tags: Classic, Heavy, and Moody

Brass is the vintage option. It has a warm gold tone that looks great on a leather collar, a weight that feels substantial, and a habit of changing color whether you approve or not.

### The good

- **Classic look.** Brass has a warm, old-school vibe. It looks like it belongs on a dog named Winston who has opinions about the weather.
- **Sturdy feel.** It's heavier and more solid-feeling than aluminum. Some people simply like a tag with heft.
- **Patina.** Over time, brass tarnishes and darkens. Some owners love this. It gives the tag character, like a well-worn pair of boots.

### The not-so-good

- **Tarnish.** Patina is charming until your dog's tag looks like a penny someone dug out of a parking lot. Keeping brass bright means polishing, and nobody has time to polish a dog tag.
- **Possible fur staining.** Tarnished brass can sometimes leave dark marks on light-colored fur where it rubs. If your dog is white or cream (hello, bulldog fawns and whites), keep an eye on it.
- **Weight and noise.** Brass is heavy and loud. Fine for big dogs, a lot for little ones.
- **Engraving contrast can vary.** Depending on the finish and how much the brass has tarnished, engraved text may not pop as much over time. Legibility is the whole point of a tag, so this matters.
- **Moisture sensitivity.** Humid climates, salt air, and regular dunking can speed up tarnish. Florida humidity doesn't negotiate.

### Best for

Larger dogs, owners who love a vintage look and don't mind some upkeep, and anyone who thinks of a patina as a feature, not a flaw.

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## Head-to-Head: Quick Comparison

Here's the short version for anyone whose dog is currently eating something they shouldn't:

| Feature | Stainless Steel | Aluminum | Brass

| Weight | Medium-heavy | Very light | Heavy

| Scratch resistance | High | Low | Medium

| Rust/corrosion resistance | High | Good, but can dull | Tarnishes

| Color options | Mostly silver/dark | Lots of colors | Gold tone

| Engraving longevity | Excellent | Good; color scuffs with wear | Varies with tarnish

| Maintenance | Almost none | Low | Polishing if you want shine

| Noise | Jingly | Quieter | Loud

| Best for | Most dogs, water dogs | Small dogs, cats | Big dogs, vintage fans

## The Florida Factor: Salt, Sun, and Pool Water

If you're in Florida, your dog's tag has a harder job than most. Salt air, constant humidity, chlorinated pools, and beach days all take a toll on metal.

For Florida dogs, especially ones who think every body of water is personally inviting them in, stainless steel is the safest bet. It handles salt and moisture better than the other two. Aluminum can work, but expect it to look more worn over time. Brass will tarnish faster in humid, salty air, so only pick it if you like the aged look.

A quick freshwater rinse after a beach day helps any tag last longer. It helps the dog too, honestly.

And a reminder from a family of bulldog owners: many bulldogs can't swim. "Can't swim. Still at the beach." is a joke on a tag, not a training plan. Life vests exist for a reason.

## What About Silencers, Size, and Shape?

The metal is only part of the decision.

- **Size:** Match the tag to your dog. A big tag on a tiny dog bounces around and can bother them. A tiny tag on a big dog is hard to read.
- **Silencers:** Rubber or silicone tag silencers wrap around the edge and cut down on jingling. They're great for stainless and brass, and they protect the engraving from rubbing too.
- **Number of tags:** If your dog wears an ID tag, a rabies tag, and a license tag, those tags hit each other constantly. That's how engraving wears down. Consider a slide-on tag or a silencer to keep the peace.
- **Attachment:** Split rings work but can snag. Check the ring regularly. A great tag doesn't help if it falls off at the dog park.

## What to Put on the Tag

Whatever metal you choose, the essentials are the same:

- Your phone number (the most important thing on the tag)
- Your dog's name, if you're comfortable sharing it
- A note like "Microchipped" if your dog is chipped
- Any medical needs, like "Needs meds"

Then, if there's room, add some personality. A tag that says "Return for reward. Reward is me." is still a functional ID tag. It just also makes whoever finds your dog laugh before they call you. That's a win.

Engraving vs. Printing, and What Actually Lasts](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/do-dog-tags-wear-off/) · [All guides →](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/) · [Build a tag →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)

Questions humans ask

## FAQ

Still stuck? [hello@saltydogtags.com](mailto:hello@saltydogtags.com). A human answers. The dogs supervise.

**Which dog tag metal lasts the longest?**

Stainless steel is generally the most durable choice. It resists scratches, rust, and corrosion better than aluminum or brass, and laser engraving on stainless tends to stay legible for a long time.

**Are aluminum dog tags bad?**

Not at all. Aluminum tags are lightweight, colorful, and affordable, which makes them great for small dogs, cats, and puppies. They're softer, though, so they scratch and scuff more easily with heavy wear.

**Do brass dog tags turn colors?**

Yes. Brass tarnishes over time and can darken or develop a patina, especially in humid or salty environments. Some people love the look. If you want it shiny, you'll need to polish it now and then.

**What's the best dog tag for a dog who swims a lot?**

Stainless steel. It handles water, salt, and chlorine better than aluminum or brass. Give it a freshwater rinse after salt water or pool time to keep it looking good.

**Is laser engraving better than stamped engraving?**

Laser engraving produces clean, precise text and fine detail, and it marks the metal directly instead of relying on paint or ink that can wear off. That's why we laser engrave every tag, including the ones that say "Snores louder than dad."

# Utah Dog License and Tag Rules (Lehi, Utah County, Salt Lake County)

> Dog license rules for Lehi and Salt Lake County, from official pages: what age, rabies proof, renewals, and how your license tag and ID tag differ.

Canonical page: https://saltydogtags.com/guides/utah-dog-license-and-tag-rules/

Salty Dog Tags · Updated Oct 13, 2026

Your dog's collar in Utah usually carries two pieces of metal with two different jobs. The **license tag** comes from your city or county and proves your dog is licensed and vaccinated. The **ID tag** is the one you buy, with your phone number on it, so whoever finds your dog can call you instead of the shelter. We make the second kind. The first kind is a government matter, so everything below comes straight from official city and county pages, linked, as checked on 2026-10-13.

Rules are set city by city. Find your city below, or call your shelter if it isn't listed.

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## Lehi

- All dogs **4 months or older** must be licensed (Lehi Municipal Code Title 6-4c-1).
- You need a **current veterinary rabies vaccination certificate** to license, and the license term can't run longer than the rabies vaccination.
- Apply online and the license tag is mailed to you, or get it in person at the **North Utah Valley Animal Shelter**, 193 N. 2000 W., Lindon.
- Lehi has a leash law: animals may not be "at large" anywhere in city limits.

Source: [Lehi City Animal Control Services](https://www.lehi-ut.gov/departments/police/animal-control-services/).

## Orem, Provo, Saratoga Springs, American Fork and the rest of Utah County

Each city sets its own licensing rules. Many north Utah County cities license through the North Utah Valley Animal Shelter (NUVAS) in Lindon; others use their own animal control or the South Utah Valley shelter. We couldn't confirm the details for these cities from an official page today, so we're not going to guess at ages, deadlines or fees. Search your city's website for "animal control," or call NUVAS or your city offices.

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## Salt Lake City and Salt Lake County

Salt Lake County Animal Services licenses pets for Salt Lake City, Bluffdale, Holladay, Midvale, Millcreek, Murray and the Metro Townships (Brighton, Copperton, County Islands, Emigration Canyon, Kearns, Magna and White City). Other cities, such as South Salt Lake, run their own programs.

- Cats, dogs and ferrets must be licensed **by 5 months of age**, or **within 30 days** of moving in or getting the pet.
- Submit **proof of vaccination** (and sterilization, if it applies). The county page doesn't name specific vaccines; ask the county.
- Licenses **renew every year**.
- Licensed pets can get a **free microchip** from the county with proof of a current license.

Source: [Salt Lake County Animal Services licensing](https://www.saltlakecounty.gov/animal-services/licensing/).

## St. George and Washington County

Southern Utah cities set their own rules, and they differ from each other: St. George renews every year, Washington City every two years, Ivins until the rabies certificate runs out. We wrote them up from the city pages in [St. George dog license rules (plus Washington City, Hurricane and Ivins)](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/st-george-dog-license-rules/).

## What goes on the collar

None of the pages above dictate what your personal ID tag has to say. They issue the license tag; the rest is up to you. Our advice, from a house where seven bulldogs have each tested the fence at least once:

- **License tag** from your city or county, so animal control can look your dog up.
- **Rabies tag**, if your vet gave you one.
- **An ID tag with your phone number**, big and readable. A license number means a phone call to a shelter during business hours. Your number means a phone call to you, right now.

**To be clear: our tags are ID tags, not license or rabies tags, and they don't satisfy any licensing requirement.** You still need the license from your city or county.

That third tag is where we come in. Name and phone number engraved on the back, something funny on the front, laser engraved in Lehi. See [what to put on a dog tag](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/what-to-put-on-a-dog-tag/) or go straight to [the builder](https://saltydogtags.com/#build).

Bonus homework: when you license, look up where to take the dog afterward. We did [Utah County dog parks](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/dog-parks-utah-county/) too.

## FAQ

Still stuck? [hello@saltydogtags.com](mailto:hello@saltydogtags.com). A human answers. The dogs supervise.

**At what age does my dog need a license in Lehi?**

Lehi requires all dogs 4 months or older to be licensed, and you need a current veterinary rabies certificate to do it. Licensing is handled through the North Utah Valley Animal Shelter in Lindon or online.

**When do I have to license a dog in Salt Lake County?**

Salt Lake County Animal Services says pets in its service area must be licensed by 5 months of age or within 30 days of moving in or getting the pet, and renewed every year.

**Is the license tag the same as an ID tag?**

No. The license tag is issued by your city or county and proves the dog is licensed. An ID tag is one you buy, engraved with your phone number so a finder can call you directly. Most owners use both.

**Does a Salty Dog Tags tag count as my dog license?**

No. Our tags are ID tags, not license or rabies tags, and they don’t satisfy any licensing requirement. Your license tag comes from your city or county.

**What about Orem, Provo or American Fork?**

Each city sets its own licensing rules, and many north Utah County cities license through the North Utah Valley Animal Shelter in Lindon. Check your city’s animal control page or call the shelter.

---

# What to Put on a Dog Tag (Without Wasting Precious Tag Real Estate)

> Phone number, medical notes, the name debate. Here's what to put on a dog tag, what to skip, and how to make it funny without making it useless.

Canonical page: https://saltydogtags.com/guides/what-to-put-on-a-dog-tag/

Salty Dog Tags · Updated Oct 12, 2026

A dog tag has one job: get your dog home. It just happens to do that job from a piece of metal smaller than a cracker, dangling off the neck of an animal who thinks the mailman is a war crime.

We know this better than most. We're a family in Lehi, Utah, living with seven English bulldogs, which means we've had plenty of practice imagining a stranger crouched on a sidewalk, holding a snorting, wheezing escape artist, squinting at a tag and trying to figure out who owns this thing. That moment is the whole reason the tag exists. Everything you engrave should help that stranger, fast.

That doesn't mean it has to be boring. It means it has to work *first*, and be funny second. Here's how to do both.

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## The Non-Negotiable: Your Phone Number

If you put only one thing on your dog's tag, make it a phone number. Not your email, not your Instagram handle, not a poem. A phone number.

Here's why: the person who finds your dog is probably standing outside, maybe in the heat, maybe in the rain, maybe on a Florida beach while your bulldog sits on their towel like he paid for it. They want to make one call and be done. Make that easy.

A few tips:

- **Use your cell, not a landline.** You want the number that rings when you're out frantically driving around the neighborhood.
- **Include the area code.** Always. Your dog might wander farther than you think, and a stranger shouldn't have to guess.
- **Add a second number if you have room.** A partner, a roommate, a trusted neighbor. If you're on a plane or in a dead zone, someone else can pick up.
- **Keep it current.** A tag with a disconnected number is just jewelry. If you change numbers, change the tag.

## Should You Put Your Dog's Name on the Tag?

This one gets debated. Some people argue that putting your dog's name on the tag lets a stranger call your dog by name, which could make it easier for a bad actor to win the dog over. Others say a name helps a good Samaritan calm a scared dog and get it to come closer.

Both sides have a point. Here's how we think about it:

- If your dog is friendly with everyone (looking at most bulldogs), the name probably doesn't change much. They'll go with anyone holding a cheese stick.
- If your dog is nervous or skittish, hearing their name from a stranger might help them settle.
- If you're worried about theft, you can leave the name off and use that space for a second phone number or a "microchipped" note instead.

There's no wrong answer. It's your dog and your call. Just don't let the name take up space your phone number needs.

## "Microchipped": Two Words That Pull Their Weight

If your dog has a microchip, say so on the tag. It tells the finder there's a backup plan: any vet or shelter can scan the dog and pull up your info. It also gently signals that this dog is somebody's, and somebody is looking.

Our [sayings list](https://saltydogtags.com/sayings/) has a tag that says it best:

**Microchipped.Still dumb.**

It's useful information delivered with honesty. Your dog's intelligence is between you and your dog.

And a reminder: a microchip only works if the registration is current. Getting the chip is step one. Updating your contact info with the chip registry when you move or change numbers is step two, and a lot of people forget step two.

## Medical Needs and Special Info

If your dog has a condition a stranger *needs* to know about, the tag is the place for it. Short and clear:

- "Needs meds"
- "Diabetic"
- "Deaf"
- "Blind"
- "Allergic to [whatever]"
- "Seizures, call ASAP"

This kind of line can change how someone handles your dog in the hour before you get there. A deaf dog won't respond to being called. A dog who needs medication on a schedule turns a lost-dog situation into an urgent one. Say it plainly. This is not the line for jokes.

Bulldog owners, you know the drill. Our dogs have opinions about heat and stairs, and a squished face that doesn't love a lot of exertion. If your dog has breathing issues or overheats easily, something like "Keep me cool" can actually help a well-meaning stranger, especially in a Florida summer.

## Address: Full, Partial, or Skip It?

A full street address used to be standard on dog tags. These days, a lot of people skip it. Your phone number does the job, and some folks just aren't comfortable putting their home address on something that dangles in public.

Middle-ground options:

- **City only.** Helpful if your dog is a traveler, like a beach-trip regular or a road-trip copilot. A finder in Destin who sees "Tampa" on the tag knows this dog is a long way from home.
- **Street name only.** Gives a finder a hint without the full picture.
- **Skip it entirely.** Totally fine if your number fits and is current.

[Make one in 2 minutes →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)or [let us roast your dog](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/) for the line.

## Rabies and License Tags

Separate from your ID tag, your dog may need to wear a rabies tag or a license tag, depending on where you live. Rules vary by state, county, and city. In Florida, rabies vaccination is required, and many counties also have licensing requirements. Check with your local county or vet so you know what applies to you.

These tags are official and they don't replace your ID tag. They have a number on them that *can* trace back to you, but usually only during business hours, through an office, after a few phone calls. Your ID tag is the fast lane. Use both.

## How Much Fits on a Dog Tag?

Less than you think. This is where most tag plans fall apart: someone writes a beautiful paragraph, then discovers they're working with a few short lines on something roughly the size of a quarter.

General guidance:

- **Keep lines short.** A handful of words per line reads best.
- **Use both sides.** Front for personality, back for contact info is a classic setup.
- **Prioritize ruthlessly.** Phone number first, critical medical info second, everything else after.
- **Bigger dog, bigger tag.** Our [bulldogs](https://saltydogtags.com/bulldog-dog-tags/) can carry a hefty tag without complaint. A Chihuahua probably shouldn't be wearing a dinner plate.

## Make It Last: Why Engraving Method Matters

A tag is only useful if a stranger can read it. Dogs scratch, dig, swim, roll in things you'd rather not identify, and drag their tags across every surface they meet. Salt water and sand are especially rough on gear. Florida beach dogs, this is about you.

That's why we laser-engrave our tags. Laser engraving gives you crisp, clean text that holds up to daily dog life far better than a cheap print that rubs off. Whatever you buy, ask how the text is applied. If a tag looks faded after a few weeks, it's not going to help much if your dog makes a break for it six months from now.

## Now for the Fun Part: Personality

Once the important stuff is covered, you've earned the right to be ridiculous. A funny tag doesn't just make you smile every time your dog trots by. It can make a stranger more likely to smile, laugh, and call. Nobody ignores a dog wearing a tag that says:

**Don't follow me.I'm lost too.**

Or the classic bulldog confession:

**Runs onnaps and spite.**

The best funny tags follow a simple rule: **setup, then punch.** Short line, shorter payoff. Some favorites from our catalog:

- **Not lost. Taking a tour.** For the dog who considers the fence a suggestion.
- **Return for reward. Reward is me.** Confidence, unearned.
- **Good boy (legally disputed).** For the dog with a record.
- **Does not come when called. Try snacks.** Funny *and* genuinely useful advice for a finder.
- **Velcro dog. Will not detach.** For the shadow that follows you to the bathroom.

Notice how some of these sneak in real info? "Try snacks" tells a stranger exactly how to catch your dog. That's the sweet spot: a joke that's also a tip.

And for the grown-ups with a saltier sense of humor, yes, we have an 18+ section. You know who you are. Just remember that kids, neighbors, and your vet's front desk will all read it eventually.

## A Simple Dog Tag Template

If you want a starting point, try this layout:

**Front:**

- Funny line (two or three short lines)

**Back:**

- Dog's name (optional)
- Phone number
- Second phone number or "Microchipped"
- Medical note (if needed)

That covers the essentials, leaves room for personality, and gives a stranger everything they need in about four seconds of reading.

Get the boring stuff right, then let your dog's true personality show. Seven bulldogs have taught us that personality is never in short supply. [Build your dog's new tag](https://saltydogtags.com/#build), or steal a line from [every saying we make](https://saltydogtags.com/sayings/).

- [Free**Roast my dog →** — One photo and a name. We write the jokes, you pick one for the tag.](https://saltydogtags.com/roast/)
- [From $12**Build a tag →** — Pick a line or write your own. Name and number go on the back.](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)

[Browse every saying →](https://saltydogtags.com/sayings/)

Engraving vs. Printing, and What Actually Lasts](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/do-dog-tags-wear-off/) · [All guides →](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/) · [Build a tag →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)

Questions humans ask

## FAQ

Still stuck? [hello@saltydogtags.com](mailto:hello@saltydogtags.com). A human answers. The dogs supervise.

**What is the most important thing to put on a dog tag?**

Your phone number, with the area code. If you only have room for one thing, that's it. A finder can call you on the spot without needing a vet, shelter, or microchip scanner.

**Should I put my dog's name on the tag?**

It's a personal choice. A name can help calm a scared dog, but some owners leave it off out of theft concerns. If space is tight, prioritize your phone number over the name.

**Is it safe to put my address on a dog tag?**

Many people now skip the full address and rely on a phone number instead. If you want to include location info, a city or street name is a reasonable middle ground.

**Do I still need an ID tag if my dog is microchipped?**

Yes. A microchip requires a scanner, usually at a vet or shelter. A tag lets anyone contact you immediately. Put "Microchipped" on the tag so finders know there's a backup.

**Can a funny dog tag still be practical?**

Absolutely. Put your contact info on the back and the joke on the front. Some of the best funny tags, like "Does not come when called. Try snacks," actually give finders useful information.

# Pomeranian Dog Tags

## Fluff eats tags. Engraving doesn't care.

A Pomeranian doesn't wear a tag so much as absorb it. The coat swallows it, the brushing drags across it, and a humid morning turns the whole dog into a damp cotton ball. Printed tags rub off under all that.

We cut the words into the metal instead of printing them on top. Nothing is painted on, so nothing peels off.

Survives the third pool-deck zoomie. And the fourth.

[How engraving holds up →](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/do-dog-tags-wear-off/)

## Which shape fits your Pomeranian

Tags here come in one size per shape, so the shape you pick is the size you get. Small collars and small necks want small tags. For a Pomeranian, start with the round, about 1.2 inches, or the heart, about 1.5 inches. Both sit flat and stay out of the way of a tiny chin. The bone and paw are also about 1.5 inches if you want the classic look. Skip the military, which is about 2 inches, and the polished bone, the biggest tag we make at 48 mm. They'll look like a dinner plate on a Pomeranian. Every shape gets the same two-sided engraving: saying on the front, name and number on the back. Pick the shape. The size comes with it.

Stainless and brass add $4, polished adds $6. The preview in the builder is exactly what we engrave.

[Pick a shape in the builder →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)

## Pomeranian tag FAQ

Still stuck? [hello@saltydogtags.com](mailto:hello@saltydogtags.com). A human answers. The dogs supervise.

**Which tag shape fits a Pomeranian?**

Tags come in one size per shape, so the shape sets the size. For a Pomeranian, start with the round (about 1.2 inches) or the heart (about 1.5 inches). Both sit flat under a small chin. The military (about 2 inches) and the polished stainless bone (48 mm) are too big for a dog this size.

**Will all that fur wear down the engraving?**

No. The words are laser engraved into the metal, not printed on top, so brushing and constant fluff contact don't wipe them off.

**Can I put my Pom's name and my phone number on the tag?**

Yes, that's the standard build. The funny saying goes on the front, and your dog's name and your phone number are engraved on the back.

**How much does a Pomeranian tag cost?**

Tags start at $12. Every one is laser engraved in Lehi, Utah.

**What happens if the engraving comes out wrong?**

If we mis-engrave it, we remake it free. Tags are engraved and shipped from Lehi, Utah in 1 to 2 business days, then USPS takes 3 to 5 days in transit. US only.

# Will not walk. Am now furniture.

> "Will not walk. Am now furniture." on a laser-engraved dog tag. Midwalk protest, now seating. Name and phone on the back, from $12.

Dog tag saying


Red bone · $14

Midway through the walk, your dog sat down and became part of the landscape. You've tried treats, encouragement and a dramatic sigh. Nothing. He's furniture now. # Dog tag sayings with attitude.

> Sassy, smug and unbothered dog tag sayings: 'Certified menace', 'Zero chill. Full chaos.' and more. Laser engraved from $12, ships from Utah.

Canonical page: https://saltydogtags.com/sayings/attitude/

38 sayings


Some dogs are sweet. Some dogs are sweet and also a menace. This page is for the second kind. These are the lines for the dog who steals the sandwich, hears cheese from three rooms away and ignores the 200 words you taught him.

Attitude tags work because they're true. Nobody has ever read "Barks first. Thinks never." and doubted it. Nobody has met a "Certified menace" and asked for proof. The tag just says out loud what the neighbors already know, and it saves you a lot of explaining at the park.

Pick one and it loads straight into the builder. Your dog's name and your phone number go on the back, engraved into the metal, not printed on it. Tags start at $12 and ship from Lehi, Utah. If we mis-engrave it, we remake it free. Choose your dog's attitude below, then give it a name.

# Bulldog life, engraved.

> Bulldog dog tag sayings about snoring, drool, loaf shape and gas, written by a family with seven English bulldogs. Engraved from $12, ships from Utah.

Canonical page: https://saltydogtags.com/sayings/bulldog-life/

26 sayings


We have seven English bulldogs, so these aren't guesses. They're field notes. The snoring is real. The drool is real. The loaf shape is real, and so is the look they give you when the walk ends and they decide to lie down in the middle of the sidewalk.

This is the big list: wrinkles, underbite, stubborn streak and the occasional gas event. "Walk ended. I lay down. Negotiate." "Face like a fist. Heart like a pillow." "Built like a loaf." If you own one, you already know which line is yours. If you're shopping for someone who does, any of them will land.

Bulldogs have thick necks and wide collars, so check the size guide before you order: the bone, heart and paw run about 1.5 inches and the military runs about 2 inches. Name and number go on the back. Mis-engrave it and we'll remake it free. Chewed it? The first replacement is $5.

# Certified cute dog tag sayings.

> Cute dog tag sayings with a bite: 'Small. Loud. Deeply loved.' 'Pocket-sized problem.' 'Smol. Loud. Yours.' Laser engraved from $12, ships from Utah.

Canonical page: https://saltydogtags.com/sayings/certified-cute/

31 sayings


Cute is a lot of pressure. Your dog has to look at you with the head tilt, carry a tiny bow, and be deeply loved on demand. The least a tag can do is back your dog up.

These sayings are the sweet end of the list, with teeth. "I'm somebody's whole heart." "Soft. Sweet. Slightly unhinged." "Cinder block head. Marshmallow heart." "Head tilt is a manipulation tactic." Cute and a little bit dangerous, which is how we like them. Wearing a bow does not make a dog harmless.

Heart and round tags suit the small ones, and the heart says it before the words do. Pick a line, add the name and your number on the back, and we engrave it in Lehi, Utah. Tags start at $12. If we mis-engrave it, we remake it free. Your dog will accept the credit.

# Family dog tag sayings.

> Dog tag sayings for the favorite, the baby and the dog with two moms: 'Mom's favorite. Dad's problem.' and more. Engraved from $12, ships from Utah.

Canonical page: https://saltydogtags.com/sayings/family/

25 sayings


Every dog has a rank in the house. Nobody agrees on it. Mom says the baby. Dad says he doesn't have a favorite, loudly, while slipping him cheese. Grandma has already decided.

These are the tags that settle it. "Mom's favorite. Dad's problem." "Has 2 moms. Both worried." "Unpaid nanny. Call my mom." Some are for the dog who runs the house. Some are for the dog who was raised by cats and is still working through it. All of them put the family on the tag, where the whole neighborhood can read it.

Pick one to load it into the builder, then swap "mom" for "dad" or "grandma" if the house runs differently. The name and your number go on the back. Three or more tags in one order get 15% off. We have seven dogs, so we checked the math.

Find your dog's rank below.

# Lost and found dog tag sayings.

> Funny lost-and-found dog tag sayings, from 'Call my mom' to 'Not lost. Taking a tour.' Your number goes on the back. Engraved from $12.

Canonical page: https://saltydogtags.com/sayings/lost-and-found/

33 sayings


Dogs wander. Bulldogs wander about forty feet and then lie down. Either way, the back of the tag does the serious work: your dog's name and your phone number, so a stranger has something to dial. The front is where we have fun.

These are our lost-and-found lines. Some are polite. Some are not. "Call my mom. She's freaking out" is for the honest owner. "Not lost. Taking a tour" is for the dog with a different story. "If found, bring snacks" sets expectations early.

Pick a line and load it into the builder. Change a word if you want. We won't be offended. The saying goes on the front, the name and number go on the back, and we send you a photo of the exact tag before it ships. Mis-engraved? We remake it free. Chewed it or lost it? The first replacement is $5 flat.

Scroll down. Find your dog's excuse.

Canonical page: https://saltydogtags.com/shih-tzu-dog-tags/

Close-up of a laser-engraved dog tag: polished stainless bone with a paw cut-out, engraved WHISKY and a phone number

Whisky's actual tag. He's a bulldog, but the laser doesn't care what breed you are.

[Build my shih tzu's tag](https://saltydogtags.com/#build) [or read all 8 shih tzu sayings](https://saltydogtags.com/shih-tzu-dog-tags/#sayings)

- **From $12 a tag** both sides engraved
- **Shipped in 1–2 business days** USPS 3–5 days, US only
- **Free remake** if we mis-engrave

## Humidity, bath day, and a tag that survives both

A shih tzu spends half its life in humid air and the other half getting blow-dried. Printed tags fade, peel and give up somewhere around the third bath.

Ours don't, because there's no ink to lose. The words are laser engraved into the metal, so shampoo and the water bowl they get their whole beard into can't touch the lettering.

Bath day, beach day, August. All fine.

[How engraving holds up →](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/do-dog-tags-wear-off/)

## Which shape fits your Shih Tzu

Tags here come in one size per shape, so the shape you pick is the size you get. Small collars and small necks want small tags. For a Shih Tzu, start with the round, about 1.2 inches, or the heart, about 1.5 inches. Both sit flat and stay out of the way of a tiny chin. The bone and paw are also about 1.5 inches if you want the classic look. Skip the military, which is about 2 inches, and the polished bone, the biggest tag we make at 48 mm. They'll look like a dinner plate on a Shih Tzu. Every shape gets the same two-sided engraving: saying on the front, name and number on the back. Pick the shape. The size comes with it.

Stainless and brass add $4, polished adds $6. The preview in the builder is exactly what we engrave.

[Pick a shape in the builder →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)

## Shih Tzu tag FAQ

Still stuck? [hello@saltydogtags.com](mailto:hello@saltydogtags.com). A human answers. The dogs supervise.

**Which tag shape fits a Shih Tzu?**

Tags come in one size per shape, so the shape sets the size. For a Shih Tzu, start with the round (about 1.2 inches) or the heart (about 1.5 inches). Both sit flat under a small chin. The military (about 2 inches) and the polished stainless bone (48 mm) are too big for a dog this size.

**Will baths, grooming and humidity ruin an engraved tag?**

No. The words are laser engraved into the metal, not printed on top, so there's no ink to wash off, fade or peel.

**Can I put my shih tzu's name and my phone number on the tag?**

Yes, that's the standard build. The funny saying goes on the front, and your dog's name and your phone number are engraved on the back.

**Will the tag get tangled in my shih tzu's hair?**

Long coats wrap around anything that dangles. Ask your groomer for a little clearance at the neck and the tag will hang where people can read it.

**What happens if the engraving comes out wrong?**

If we mis-engrave it, we remake it free. Tags are engraved and shipped from Lehi, Utah in 1 to 2 business days, then USPS takes 3 to 5 days in transit. US only.

## Built for baths, bows and humidity

Yorkies get groomed more than most people. Baths, blow-dries, leave-in spray, the little top-knot bow. A printed tag gives up fast under all that.

Ours are laser engraved, so the words are cut into the metal instead of painted on top. No ink to wash off, flake off, or get chewed off by a jealous sibling.

Survives the spa schedule.

[How engraving holds up →](https://saltydogtags.com/guides/do-dog-tags-wear-off/)

## Which shape fits your Yorkie

Tags here come in one size per shape, so the shape you pick is the size you get. Small collars and small necks want small tags. For a Yorkie, start with the round, about 1.2 inches, or the heart, about 1.5 inches. Both sit flat and stay out of the way of a tiny chin. The bone and paw are also about 1.5 inches if you want the classic look. Skip the military, which is about 2 inches, and the polished bone, the biggest tag we make at 48 mm. They'll look like a dinner plate on a Yorkie. Every shape gets the same two-sided engraving: saying on the front, name and number on the back. Pick the shape. The size comes with it.

Stainless and brass add $4, polished adds $6. The preview in the builder is exactly what we engrave.

[Pick a shape in the builder →](https://saltydogtags.com/#build)

## Yorkie tag FAQ

Still stuck? [hello@saltydogtags.com](mailto:hello@saltydogtags.com). A human answers. The dogs supervise.

**Which tag shape fits a Yorkie?**

Tags come in one size per shape, so the shape sets the size. For a Yorkie, start with the round (about 1.2 inches) or the heart (about 1.5 inches). Both sit flat under a small chin. The military (about 2 inches) and the polished stainless bone (48 mm) are too big for a dog this size.

**Will baths and grooming ruin an engraved yorkie tag?**

No. The words are laser engraved into the metal, not printed on the surface, so shampoo, blow-dryers and humidity have nothing to peel off.

**Can I put my yorkie's name and my phone number on the tag?**

Yes, that's the standard build. The funny saying goes on the front, and your dog's name and your phone number are engraved on the back.

**Do you have sayings written specifically for yorkies?**

Eight on this page, about the size, the bark, the grooming and the refusal to walk anywhere. Or type your own in the builder and see what fits.

**What happens if the engraving comes out wrong?**

If we mis-engrave it, we remake it free. Tags are engraved and shipped from Lehi, Utah in 1 to 2 business days, then USPS takes 3 to 5 days in transit. US only.
